password_hash.description: The bcrypt hash of the user's password, as fit hash-password or htpasswd -B makes it.

username.description: The user's name; it may not contain a colon.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes the zone keeps on disk; past it the least recently used responses go. 1 GiB when left out or 0.

max_entries.description: The most responses the zone keeps on disk, which bounds the memory their index takes, a few hundred bytes each. 100000 when left out or 0.

max_size.description: Renamed max_bytes; the old name goes in config version 2.

path.description: The directory the zone's responses are kept in, made if it is missing. It is the zone's alone: no other zone may name it. What it holds is found again when fit starts.

ca_file.description: A PEM file of the certificates the directory's is checked against, in place of the system's roots, for a CA of one's own.

challenges.description: The challenges answered, in the order tried: http-01, which the CA checks on port 80 at the name, answered by any listener of fit's in the clear, and tls-alpn-01, which it checks on port 443, answered by the TLS listener that lists the name. A failed attempt is tried again with the next. Both, http-01 first, when left out.

directory.description: The URL of the CA's ACME directory. Let's Encrypt's when left out; https://acme-staging-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory is its staging CA, for tests.

email.description: The address the CA may write to about the account's certificates; none when left out.

max_concurrent.description: How many certificates are obtained at once; the rest wait their turn. 2 when left out or 0.

on_demand.description: How certificates are obtained during handshakes, for listeners whose tls sets on_demand: whom to ask whether a name may have one, and how fast and how many.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to the CA may take. 30s when left out.

shared_storage.description: Keep accounts, keys and certificates in Redis, etcd or Consul instead of a directory, for instances of fit on several hosts: one instance obtains a certificate, holding a lock there, and the others take it from there; each challenge's answer is kept there too, so that whichever instance the CA reaches answers it. Not with storage.

storage.description: The directory accounts, keys and certificates are kept in, which instances of fit may share. $XDG_DATA_HOME/fit, or ~/.local/share/fit, when left out.

timeout.description: How long obtaining one certificate may take, challenges included, before it is given up and tried again later. 10m when left out.

allow.description: IP addresses and CIDR prefixes served, as "10.0.0.0/8" or "2001:db8::/32": with any entry here or in allow_files, every address neither holds is refused, unless deny refuses it first.

allow_files.description: Files of more allow entries: an address or prefix on each line, with blank lines and what follows # or ; left out, as the lists published for firewalls are written. Read when the config is applied, and applied again when one changes; each at most 64 MiB.

deny.description: IP addresses and CIDR prefixes refused, whatever allow holds.

deny_files.description: Files of more deny entries, written as allow_files.

buffer_bytes.description: How many bytes of lines may wait to be written; lines past it are dropped. 4 MiB when left out.

flush_interval.description: How long a line may wait in the buffer before it is written; 1s when left out.

format.description: How a request's line is written, with the same fields whichever: json, a JSON object; text, time, level, msg and the fields as key=value (logfmt); or line, the time and level, then the fields as key=value, as fit's own log writes lines. A request's level is its status's, as level says. json when left out. A change takes a restart.

level.description: The least level of the requests written: a response with a status below 400 is info, a 4xx warn and a 5xx error, so warn writes the requests answered with 4xx and 5xx, and error those answered with 5xx. Every request when left out. A change takes effect on reload.

output.description: "stdout", "stderr", or the path of a file lines are appended to; "stdout" when left out.

rotate.description: Rotate the file output names, and remove old rotated files: the size and interval a file is rotated at, and the age, count and total size past which rotated files are removed. None when left out: the file grows without bound, as before.

time_zone.description: The zone a line's time is written in, and the zone a file's interval is rotated at: local (the default), utc, or an IANA zone name such as Asia/Shanghai. json and text wrote UTC and line local before this setting; now every format writes this zone, local when left out, and 24h turns at local midnight. A change takes effect on reload.

address.description: Where the Admin API listens: a host and port, or "unix/" and the path of a Unix socket, as in "unix//run/fit/admin.sock". A host that is not a loopback address or localhost needs token_file, cert_file and key_file, so that only holders of the token reach the API and the token never crosses a network in the clear. 127.0.0.1:2019 when left out.

assistant.description: The workbench's assistant, a chat beside the console's pages that reads what fit does and drafts changes for a person to submit, calling the model APIs set here; off when left out, and then nothing is sent anywhere. Needs console. With a store, these settings are the first ones only: once the Settings page saves, the store's are used, keys included.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the Admin API's certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the API is served over TLS, 1.2 or later. The files are read again when they change, so that a renewed certificate is served without a restart. Not for a Unix socket.

client_ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs that clients' certificates must chain to: with it, every client must present a valid certificate, besides the token, before it is heard. Needs cert_file and key_file; read again when it changes, as they are.

cluster.description: Manage other fits from this one, the manager: their addresses and credentials, added on the workbench's Cluster pages, are kept in the store, and each one's state is read every poll_interval. Off when left out, and then nothing is called. Needs store and console. See decision 033.

cluster_member.description: Link this fit out to a manager of many fits, which then manages it through the link as it manages others over HTTP: for a fit behind NAT, or with no port open to the manager. The manager's Add by enrollment gives the line to paste here. Off when left out, and then nothing is dialed. Read when fit starts. See decision 033.

console.description: Serve the console, web pages behind a user name and password from which the whole config, admin aside, is read and changed; off when left out.

disable_dashboard.description: Do not serve the dashboard, the read-only web pages at /dashboard/ that show the routes, services, upstreams and their health, certificates and config versions from the Admin API's GET endpoints; served when left out or false.

history.description: How many of the configs applied, the running one included, are kept to be read back. 10 when left out or 0.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate's private key.

max_config_bytes.description: The largest config the Admin API takes; a larger one gets 413. 4 MiB when left out or 0.

max_conns.description: The most connections the Admin API keeps open at once, a quarter of them kept for those that have made a request with the token (any request, without token_file). When they are taken, a new connection closes the oldest of those that have not, of the client holding the most, and is closed as it is accepted only when every one has; one past a client's share, a quarter of them, is closed too, but for loopback clients. A connection that has not is closed 5s after it is accepted, whatever it is doing. 16 when left out or 0.

mptcp.description: Listen the Admin API with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default; a Unix socket has no paths.

node_id.description: This fit's node ID, which the Admin API's GET /node answers and a manager of many fits knows it by: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', starting with a letter or digit. Left out, fit makes one, a random UUID, once, and keeps it in the store, or without one in a file beside the config, as fit.node-id beside fit.json; set it where neither lasts, as in a container whose config is read-only.

store.description: Keep the config encrypted in a file of its own, the store, which is the base config fit runs from then on: every config applied is written to it, and what this file sets beside admin is only the store's first content, used when the store does not exist yet. Left out, the config lives in this file.

token_file.description: A file holding a token that every request must carry, as "Authorization: Bearer <token>"; no token is asked for when left out.

data.description: What of fit's logs may be sent to a model, and more of what is redacted before anything is.

default_level.description: The level of a console user that users does not list: off, read (the read tools only), edit (also drafts on the open page, never submitted), propose (also proposals) or apply (also applies them). read when left out.

default_model.description: The provider and model the chat uses; the first model of the first provider when left out.

limits.description: Bounds on the assistant's conversations, tool calls and model answers; the defaults when left out.

mcp.description: An MCP server at /mcp on the console's address, for outside agents (Claude Code, Cursor, an SDK's client) to call the assistant's tools, read the config, the schema and the docs, and use the skills as prompts, with the MCP tokens users make on the workbench's MCP page. A token has its user's level, at most propose: what it proposes is applied only in the workbench. Off when left out.

params.description: What a model call asks for: its output, temperature and thinking.

providers.description: The model APIs the assistant may call, each by name. Their keys are not written here: the Settings page keeps them in admin.store, or api_key_env names a variable that holds one.

users.description: What each console user may have the assistant do, by user name; a user not listed has default_level.

redact.description: Regular expressions (Go's syntax) whose matches are replaced in everything the tools hand a model, beside the keys, hashes, tokens and private keys that always are.

send_access_log.description: Let the tools hand lines of the access log to the model, redacted. Off by default.

send_logs.description: Let the tools hand lines of fit's own log to the model, redacted. Off by default.

send_subjects.description: Let the media tools hand playback sessions' subjects to the model as they are. Off by default: each subject is replaced by a hash of it, the same for one subject while fit runs, which the propose tools take back.

max_audit_entries.description: The most entries the assistant's audit log keeps; one more removes the oldest. 1000 when left out or 0.

max_concurrent_chats.description: The most answers being made at once, across users; one more is refused until one ends. 4 when left out or 0.

max_conversations.description: The most conversations kept for each user; one more removes the oldest. 50 when left out or 0.

max_stream_bytes.description: The most bytes of one model answer as it streams in; a larger one is cut and fails. 8 MiB when left out or 0.

max_tokens_per_day.description: The most tokens, in and out, one user's calls may take in a day, as the APIs count them. 1000000 when left out or 0.

max_tool_calls.description: The most tools an answer may call before the assistant stops it. 16 when left out or 0.

max_tool_result_bytes.description: The most bytes of a tool's result handed to the model; a longer one is cut, and says so. 32 KiB when left out or 0.

max_turns.description: The most turns a conversation keeps, a user's message and the answer to it each. 40 when left out or 0.

allow.description: The addresses (as 127.0.0.1) and prefixes (as 10.0.0.0/8) MCP clients may call from; a token may narrow them further. Loopback only when left out.

max_calls_per_minute.description: The most requests of one token in a minute; past it they are answered 429 until the minute's share comes back. 120 when left out or 0.

max_concurrent_calls.description: The most requests of one token served at once; one more is answered 429. 4 when left out or 0.

max_request_bytes.description: The most bytes of a request's body, beside the console's own bound. 1 MiB when left out or 0.

max_sessions.description: The most sessions a token keeps for clients of the protocol's versions before 2026-07-28, which open one with initialize; one more ends the one used least recently. 4 when left out or 0.

max_token_days.description: The longest a token may last, in days, from when it is made. 90 when left out or 0.

max_tokens_per_user.description: The most MCP tokens a console user may hold. 10 when left out or 0.

session_idle_timeout.description: How long such a session is kept without a request. 1h when left out.

context.description: The model's context window, in tokens; 0 or left out when not known.

name.description: The model's ID, as the provider names it.

tools.description: Whether the model calls tools. On when left out.

max_output_tokens.description: The most tokens a model's answer may have. 4096 when left out or 0.

temperature.description: The sampling temperature; the model's own when left out.

thinking.description: How much a model that thinks before it answers may: off, low, medium or high, as its API takes it (an effort, or a budget of tokens). off when left out.

api_key_env.description: An environment variable holding the API key, read when a call is made; a key the Settings page keeps in the store comes first.

api_version.description: The api-version of an azure_openai provider's calls, as 2024-10-21; needed for it, and for no other kind.

base_url.description: The API's base URL, as https://api.openai.com/v1; the vendor's when left out, and needed for openai_compatible and azure_openai. Not for llm_proxy. A key is sent only over https, or to a loopback host.

connect_timeout.description: How long a connect, TLS included, may take. 10s when left out.

first_byte_timeout.description: How long a call may wait for its answer to begin. 2m when left out.

headers.description: Headers sent with every call, as an organization or a gateway's own; not the key's headers, Host or the body's framing.

idle_timeout.description: How long a streamed answer may go silent. 1m when left out.

kind.description: The API it speaks: anthropic (Messages), openai (Chat Completions), openai_responses (Responses), gemini (generateContent), azure_openai (Chat Completions of a deployment), ollama (/api/chat), openai_compatible (Chat Completions at any base_url, as vLLM, llama.cpp, DeepSeek or a gateway), or llm_proxy, this fit's own llm.proxy, reached on its api address, so that the assistant uses the mesh's models.

models.description: The models offered from this provider; the Settings page reads the provider's own list to add them.

name.description: The provider's name, which default_model and the Settings page name it by: letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'.

retries.description: How often a call is tried again when it failed before any of its answer was taken: the connect failed, or the API answered 408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504 or 529. 2 when left out; 0 tries once.

timeout.description: The most one call may take, to the end of its answer. 10m when left out.

level.description: What the user may have the assistant do: off, read, edit, propose or apply, each including the ones before it.

disable.description: Turn HTTPS by default off: no listeners are made for a config that writes none, and an empty tls gets no certificates.

disable_redirects.description: Make no listener in the clear to redirect to HTTPS. ACME's HTTP-01 challenge is then answered by none, and certificates come through TLS-ALPN-01.

http_port.description: The port of the listener in the clear that redirects to HTTPS. 80 when left out or 0.

https_port.description: The port of the HTTPS listener, and the one redirects name when it is not 443. 443 when left out or 0.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate, followed by any intermediates.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate's private key.

at.description: When the slot starts, in the channel's time_zone: HH:MM or HH:MM:SS every day; days of the week before it, as mon,wed,fri 20:00 or sat-sun 09:30; or a date, as 2026-12-31 23:00, once.

item.description: The ID of the library's item the slot plays, from its start.

ca_files.description: PEM files of the certificate authorities a client's certificate must chain to. They are watched as certificate files are: a change loads the config again.

mode.description: require: a client without a valid certificate is refused in the handshake; verify_if_given: a client may send none, and a route that needs one says so with the client_cert middleware, but one it sends must be valid. require when left out. A listener that requires certificates cannot answer ACME's TLS-ALPN-01 challenge, whose CA sends none.

admins.description: Console users (admin.console.users) who are the cluster's admins whatever roles the Users and audit page gives: the way back in when no admin is left. Once this or a role is set, a console user does on the cluster what its roles let it, and only a cluster-wide admin changes this manager's own config; until then, every console user is a cluster-wide admin. Changed at a restart, as all of admin is.

link_address.description: Where members that link out to the manager reach it, as ":7444" or "0.0.0.0:7444": a WebSocket listener over TLS, with a self-signed certificate the manager makes once and keeps in the store, which each member pins when it enrolls. Members behind NAT, or with no port open, link here with the config line Add by enrollment gives, and are managed through their link as the others are over HTTP. Off when left out: no member can enroll.

link_url.description: The URL members reach link_address at, as "wss://manager.example.com:7444/cluster/link", which the config line Add by enrollment gives names; when left out, the host the page was opened at and link_address's port. Only a wss URL.

max_concurrency.description: The most members polled at once; the others wait for their turn. Tests from the pages run beside them, 4 at most. Each operation on many members (reload, rollback, check, purge, test) calls at most this many of them at once too. 8 when left out or 0.

max_nodes.description: The most members the manager keeps; one more is refused. 256 when left out or 0.

max_response_bytes.description: The largest answer read from a member; a larger one fails its call, and is reported as too large. 4 MiB when left out or 0; 16 KiB at least.

poll_interval.description: How often each member's GET /node, /status and /config/check are read. 10s when left out; 1s at least.

timeout.description: The longest one call to a member may take, from its connect to the last byte of its answer; the connect and the wait for the answer's header are bounded by it too. 10s when left out; 1s at least.

fingerprint.description: The SHA-256 of the manager's link certificate, 64 hex digits, with or without colons, as the page gives it: the only certificate this fit links to.

manager.description: The manager's link URL, as its Add by enrollment page gives it: wss://host:port/cluster/link.

token.description: The enrollment token the manager made for this fit, fite1.<ID>.<secret>, used once: this fit proves it to the manager, which answers a credential of this fit's own, kept in the store, or without one in a file beside the config (fit.cluster-member beside fit.json); the token is not used again. Left out once this fit has a credential; a new token enrolls this fit again.

token_file.description: A file holding the enrollment token, in place of token.

address.description: The host and port the console listens on. A host that is not a loopback address needs cert_file and key_file, so that passwords never cross a network in the clear. 127.0.0.1:2020 when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the console's certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the console is served over TLS.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate's private key.

max_conns.description: The most connections the console keeps open at once, a quarter of them kept for those with a login. When they are taken, a new connection closes the oldest of those without one, of the client holding the most, and is closed as it is accepted only when every one has a login; one past a client's share, a quarter of them, is closed too, but for loopback clients. 32 when left out or 0.

max_sessions.description: The most logins kept at once; one more ends the oldest. 64 when left out or 0.

mptcp.description: Listen the console with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default.

session_lifetime.description: How long a login lasts at most, however busy. 12h when left out.

session_timeout.description: How long a login lasts without a request. 30m when left out.

users.description: Who may log in: at least one user.

password_hash.description: The bcrypt hash of the user's password, as fit hash-password makes it.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs Consul's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https, as Consul's verify_incoming asks for; with key_file.

datacenter.description: The datacenter whose KV store is read; the agent's when left out.

endpoint.description: Where Consul's HTTP API is, as of the local agent: http:// or https:// and a host and port. http://127.0.0.1:8500 when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

max_keys.description: The most keys taken; past it, the rest, by key, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0.

prefix.description: The keys read are those starting with it. Each holds a JSON object of listeners, routes, upstreams and services, as a config holds them; keys ending in '/' and empty ones are passed over, and a key whose value is not such an object is left out and reported. fit/ when left out.

refresh_interval.description: How often what the keys provide is sent again whether or not it changed, so that a part refused because of the rest of the config is tried again. 30s when left out.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to Consul may take, connecting included, beyond the five minutes a blocking query waits for a change. 10s when left out.

token_file.description: A file holding the ACL token to send, read each time a watch starts; none when left out. The token needs to read the keys under prefix.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs Consul's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https, as Consul's verify_incoming asks for; with key_file.

datacenter.description: The datacenter whose catalog is read; the agent's when left out.

endpoint.description: Where Consul's HTTP API is, as of the local agent: http:// or https:// and a host and port. http://127.0.0.1:8500 when left out.

expose_all.description: Take every service in the catalog; only those tagged <tag_prefix>.enable=true when left out or false. An instance tagged <tag_prefix>.enable=false is never taken.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

max_services.description: The most services taken; past it, the rest, by name, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0.

refresh_interval.description: How often the catalog is read again whether or not it changed. 30s when left out.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to Consul may take, connecting included, beyond the five minutes a blocking query waits for a change. 10s when left out.

tag_prefix.description: What the tags read start with, as in fit.routes.web.host=example.com; tags without '=' are passed over. Besides the routes, services and upstream settings a Docker container's labels may set, <tag_prefix>.name names the upstream, the service's name when left out. fit when left out.

token_file.description: A file holding the ACL token to send, read each time a watch starts; none when left out. The token needs to read the services and nodes served.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs Consul's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https; with key_file.

datacenter.description: The datacenter whose KV store is used; the agent's when left out.

endpoint.description: Where Consul's HTTP API is, as of the local agent: http:// or https:// and a host and port. http://127.0.0.1:8500 when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

token_file.description: A file holding the ACL token to send, read when fit starts; none when left out. The token needs to read and write the keys under prefix and to make sessions.

endpoint.description: Where the Docker daemon's API is: unix:// and a socket's path, or tcp:// and a host and port, as of a socket proxy, in plain HTTP. unix:///var/run/docker.sock when left out.

expose_all.description: Take every running container with routes or services in its labels; only those labelled <label_prefix>.enable=true when left out or false. A container labelled <label_prefix>.enable=false is never taken.

label_prefix.description: What the labels read start with, as in fit.routes.web.host. fit when left out.

max_containers.description: The most containers taken; past it, the rest, by name, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0.

network.description: The Docker network whose address of a container's is used, when the container is on several and has no <label_prefix>.network label; the first by name when left out.

refresh_interval.description: How often the containers are listed again whether or not an event came, in case one was missed. 30s when left out.

request_timeout.description: How long listing the containers may take, connecting included. 10s when left out.

use_published_ports.description: Send to the port a container's port is published on, on the host, rather than to the container's own address: for a fit outside Docker that cannot reach containers' addresses, as on Docker Desktop.

backlog.description: The length of each listening socket's queue of connections not yet accepted. The system's when left out or 0.

event_loops.description: How many event loops each engine waits for its connections' events on, which spread the waits, accepts and wake-ups over cores; the connections' work runs on the workers either way. fib's default when left out or 0: 1 on up to 4 CPUs, 2 on up to 16, and the CPUs divided by 8 on more. Windows has one loop whatever this says.

loop_wait.description: How each event loop waits while none of its connections has an event ready: park, in Go's network poller, which gives the loop's CPU to other work at once, but on a busy server looks for the loop's events only when a CPU runs out of work or every 10ms; or block, in epoll_wait, which wakes the loop as soon as one arrives. Choose block for a shorter latency tail near saturation over HTTP/1.1, at the cost of the median and a little h2 throughput: proxying an API at 200,000 requests a second on 6 CPUs, block took the HTTP/1.1 p99 from 4.3 to 2.9-3.9ms and the median from 0.95 to 1.57ms, left h2 and the maximum as they were, and served h2 0.9% less at saturation. Linux only. park when left out.

min_workers.description: How many workers an idle pool keeps, rather than retiring every one and starting them again when work arrives. None when left out or 0.

poll_batch.description: The most events one wait of an event loop collects; the rest wait for the next. 1024 when left out or 0.

read_buffer_size.description: The bytes a connection reads its socket into at a time, which is also the most a proxied body is passed on in one write. 64 KiB when left out or 0.

task_queue.description: How many tasks each engine's pool holds waiting for a worker. fib's default, which follows its workers, when left out or 0.

workers.description: The most workers each engine's pool runs connections' reads and callbacks on at once. 100 for each CPU fit may use, and at least min_workers, when left out or 0.

write_watermark.description: The bytes a connection may have waiting to be written before it stops reading until they drain, the backpressure on one connection; limits.max_pending_bytes bounds them all together. When left out or 0, fib sizes it from read_buffer_size and the machine: four read buffers, at least 64 KiB and at most 256 KiB, so 256 KiB at the default 64 KiB read buffer on a machine with enough memory.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs etcd's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https, as etcd's client-cert-auth asks for; with key_file.

endpoints.description: Where etcd's client API is: http:// or https:// and a host and port, for each member to try, in turn when one fails. http://127.0.0.1:2379 when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

max_keys.description: The most keys taken; past it, the rest, by key, are left out and reported. 1000 when left out or 0.

password_file.description: A file holding username's password, read each time a watch starts.

prefix.description: The keys read are those starting with it. Each holds a JSON object of listeners, routes, upstreams and services, as a config holds them; keys ending in '/' and empty ones are passed over, and a key whose value is not such an object is left out and reported. fit/ when left out.

refresh_interval.description: How often the keys are read again whether or not a watch event came. 30s when left out.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to etcd may take, connecting included, and a watch to start; a watch then lasts until it fails. 10s when left out.

username.description: The user to authenticate as, with password_file, when etcd's authentication is on; none when left out.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs etcd's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https; with key_file.

endpoints.description: Where etcd's client API is: http:// or https:// and a host and port, for each member to try, in turn when one fails. http://127.0.0.1:2379 when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

password_file.description: A file holding username's password, read each time fit authenticates.

username.description: The user to authenticate as, with password_file, when etcd's authentication is on; none when left out.

allow.description: The destinations the proxy connects to: host names, "*.example.com" for every name below example.com, IP addresses and CIDR ranges, which also hold the address a host name resolves to. Every destination deny does not hold when left out, but for loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, the metadata service of most clouds, among them), unspecified and multicast addresses and the host's own, which are refused unless a range here lies inside theirs, as "127.0.0.0/8" does and "0.0.0.0/0" does not, or, for the host's own, names that address alone.

clients.description: The addresses and CIDR ranges of the clients that may use the proxy, as "10.0.0.0/8"; others are refused.

connect_timeout.description: How long resolving and connecting to a destination may take. 10s when left out.

deny.description: Destinations refused, written as in allow, whatever allow holds: a host name that resolves to an address deny holds is refused once it is connected, before anything is sent.

idle_timeout.description: How long a proxied connection may carry nothing either way before both sides are closed. 5m when left out.

ports.description: The destination ports allowed; any when left out.

expect_status.description: With http: the statuses that pass; any from 200 to 399 when left out.

fails.description: How many probes in a row must fail to take an address out of rotation; 2 when left out or 0.

host.description: With http: the Host field the probe sends; the address's host when left out.

interval.description: How long from the start of one probe of an address to the start of the next; 5s when left out.

jitter.description: Up to how much longer than interval each wait between probes may be, chosen at random each time, so that probes from many upstreams spread out; a tenth of interval when left out. Less than interval.

passes.description: How many probes in a row must pass to put an address that was out back in; 2 when left out or 0.

path.description: With http: the path, and query, the probe asks for; / when left out.

port.description: The port probes go to, in place of each address's own.

timeout.description: How long a probe may take, connecting included, before it fails; 2s when left out. No longer than interval.

type.description: http sends a GET request, over the upstream's protocol, and passes on an expected status; tcp passes once a connection opens. http when left out.

urls.description: The server's stun:, stuns:, turn: or turns: URLs.

http_port.description: The port Ingresses' rules are served on over HTTP. 80 when left out or 0.

https_port.description: The port the hosts of Ingresses' tls are served on over HTTPS. 443 when left out or 0.

addresses.description: The addresses where clients reach fit's Gateways, IP addresses or host names, written into each one's status.addresses, as clients of the Gateway API and its conformance tests read them. None are written when left out, and those there are kept.

allow_external_name_services.description: Send requests to the backends of ExternalName Services, to the host name each names, refusing one that is loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, the metadata service of most clouds, among them), unspecified or multicast, by address or by the address the name resolves to, or the host's own: whoever may create a Service could otherwise point a route at fit's Admin API or the cloud's metadata service. Off when left out: a backend that is an ExternalName Service is not resolved, and its route says so in its status.

backends.description: Where requests to a Service go: endpoints, to its ready endpoints from its EndpointSlices, balanced by fit; or cluster_ip, to its cluster IP, balanced by the cluster. endpoints when left out.

certificates_dir.description: The directory the certificates of HTTPS listeners are written to, from the Secrets they name, for fit's TLS to load: each Secret's chain and key in one file only fit's user may read, named for the Secret and a hash of its contents. Files of that form that are no longer named are removed. A directory of fit's own in the system's temporary directory, removed when fit stops, when left out.

context.description: The kubeconfig's context to use; its current-context when left out.

controller_name.description: The controllerName of the GatewayClasses whose Gateways fit serves. lesismal.github.io/fit when left out.

ingress.description: Serve Ingresses too: those whose ingressClassName, or kubernetes.io/ingress.class annotation, names an IngressClass whose controller is controller_name, and those naming none when such a class is the default. Their rules are served on http_port, and on https_port for the hosts of their tls, with the certificates of its Secrets. fit's account then needs to list and watch Ingresses and IngressClasses. No Ingresses when left out.

kubeconfig.description: A kubeconfig file to reach the cluster with: its server, CA, client certificate, token or token file. When left out, the pod's service account, inside the cluster, or else $KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config. Exec and auth-provider plugins are not supported.

listen_host.description: The IP address Gateway listeners are bound on, each on its port; every address when left out.

max_objects.description: The most objects of each kind kept: past it, the rest are left out and reported. 10000 when left out or 0.

namespaces.description: The namespaces whose Gateways and routes are served; every namespace when left out. Resources are watched across the cluster either way, so fit's account needs to list and watch them cluster-wide, Secrets of type kubernetes.io/tls among them, and to patch the status of GatewayClasses, Gateways and routes.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to the API server may take, but watches, which last five minutes each. 10s when left out.

hub.description: Run a hub: nodes and proxies link to it, and it passes calls between them.

node.description: Run a node: it serves models from local or remote upstreams to the hubs and proxies linked to it.

proxy.description: Run a proxy: an OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API, for agents, that calls the models of the nodes it reaches.

console.description: The hub's web pages; none when left out.

id.description: The hub's stable ID, which its peers know it by. Made when left out, and written back here.

limits.description: Bounds on the hub's links; the defaults when left out.

listen.description: Where the hub takes links from nodes and proxies; none when left out. Its pages change it.

max_nodes.description: The most nodes the hub keeps in its table, offline ones included; past it the offline node seen longest ago is forgotten; online nodes are bounded by limits.max_conns and the hub's peers. 1024 when left out or 0.

name.description: The name the hub shows its peers; the host's name when left out. Its pages change it.

peers.description: The nodes and proxies the hub dials. Its pages change them.

tokens.description: The tokens the hub's listener issued, which nodes and proxies link with in place of a password: each its own credential, of no role, kept as a hash, with an optional expiry. The pages, the Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand.

max_conns.description: The most links the role takes from its peers at once; one past it is refused, and its dialer backs off. 1024 when left out or 0.

max_inflight.description: The most calls and streams a peer may have running here on one link at once; one past it fails at once. 1024 when left out or 0.

ping_interval.description: How long a link may hear nothing before it is pinged; one that hears nothing for three of them is closed. 15s when left out.

retry_interval.description: The most a dialer waits between attempts at a peer it cannot reach; the waits grow to it, at random within each step. 5s when left out.

slow_timeout.description: How long a ping may wait for its pong, behind everything sent before it, before the link is taken for too slow and closed. 30s when left out.

stream_idle.description: How long a stream, as a model call relayed between roles, may carry nothing either way before it ends. 2m when left out.

address.description: The host and port the role takes links on, as a binding of its own on the listeners' engine; the WebSocket path is /ws. An empty host listens on every address.

cert.description: The PEM certificate self_signed made; with key. Written by the role; delete both for a new one, which every peer must pin again.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate the listener presents, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, links are taken over TLS (wss://), and peers check it with their ca_file or pin. A listener on an address other than a loopback one needs TLS: this, or self_signed. Read when the listener starts, and again when it changes on disk (fit run -watch-certs): links from then on are taken with the new certificate, and those open stay.

hub_password.description: The password hubs prove to link as a hub, on a node's or a proxy's listener; password when left out.

key.description: The PEM private key of cert.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the private key of cert_file.

node_password.description: The password nodes prove to link as a node, on a hub's or a proxy's listener; password when left out.

password.description: The password of every role the listener links with that has no password of its own: peers prove they know it when they link, and it never crosses the network. Whoever holds it may link as any of those roles, so give each role its own instead. None when left out.

proxy_password.description: The password proxies prove to link as a proxy, on a hub's or a node's listener; password when left out.

self_signed.description: Take links over TLS (wss://) with a self-signed certificate the role makes and keeps, so that it outlives a restart: in cert and key with admin.store, or else in a file beside the config, 0600, as fit.llm.hub.pem beside fit.json; its pages and its log show its SHA-256 fingerprint, which peers set as their pin. For a listener without cert_file.

api.description: The API the upstream speaks: openai (OpenAI and every OpenAI-compatible server, as DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Groq, xAI, OpenRouter, vLLM, llama.cpp), anthropic, gemini (Google's Gemini API), azure_openai (Azure OpenAI deployments, which agents call as openai), ollama (Ollama's own API) or cohere (Cohere's v2 API). It sets the agent endpoints the model is reached through, the upstream URL and the auth header.

api_key.description: The key sent upstream: as Authorization: Bearer for openai, ollama and cohere, as x-api-key for anthropic, x-goog-api-key for gemini, api-key for azure_openai. None when left out. The pages never show it whole.

api_version.description: The api-version query every call of an azure_openai model carries, as 2024-10-21: required for azure_openai, and only taken there.

base_url.description: The upstream's base URL, http or https, without a query or a trailing slash. openai, anthropic and cohere calls go to it with their path appended, as base_url/chat/completions with http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1; gemini's to base_url/models/{upstream}:{method}, with https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta; azure_openai's to base_url/openai/deployments/{upstream}/{path}, with https://{resource}.openai.azure.com; ollama's to base_url/api/chat, with http://127.0.0.1:11434.

description.description: A note about the model its peers show.

disabled.description: Keep the model without serving it.

max_inflight.description: The most calls to the model the node forwards at once; a call past it goes to another node. No bound but proxy.max_inflight's when left out or 0.

name.description: The name agents ask for the model by: 1 to 128 characters, no spaces. A name is unique among a node's models of one agent API: an azure_openai model shares openai's.

upstream.description: The model ID sent upstream in place of name: in the body's model, a form's model field, Gemini's path, or as an azure_openai model's deployment. name when left out.

console.description: The node's web pages; none when left out.

description.description: A note about the node its peers show. Its pages, and a hub that settings.allow_hub_manage lets, change it.

id.description: The node's stable ID, which its peers know it by. Made when left out, and written back here.

limits.description: Bounds on the node's links; the defaults when left out.

listen.description: Where the node takes links from hubs and proxies; none when left out. Its pages change it.

models.description: The models the node serves: each an upstream API endpoint. Its pages, and a hub that settings.allow_hub_manage lets, change them.

name.description: The name the node shows its peers; the host's name when left out. Its pages, and a hub that settings.allow_hub_manage lets, change it.

peers.description: The hubs and proxies the node dials. Its pages change them.

proxy.description: Bounds on the calls the node forwards to its models' upstreams; the defaults when left out.

settings.description: The node's own settings; the defaults when left out. Only its own pages change them.

tokens.description: The tokens the node's listener issued, which hubs and proxies link with in place of a password: each its own credential, of no role, kept as a hash, with an optional expiry. The pages, the Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand.

connect_timeout.description: How long a connection to an upstream may take. 10s when left out.

first_byte_timeout.description: How long an upstream may take to begin its response, from when the call starts, its connect included, as a model reading a long prompt does. 5m when left out.

idle_timeout.description: How long an upstream may go silent in the middle of its response before the call is cut short. 5m when left out.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest request body a call may carry; one past it fails. A body is held whole only when the model's upstream differs from the name the call gives and the model is named in the body (its JSON model, or a form's model field), to set it. 32 MiB when left out or 0.

max_inflight.description: The most calls the node forwards at once, across its models; a call past it goes to another node. 256 when left out or 0.

timeout.description: The most one call may take, from its start to the end of its response. 30m when left out.

allow_hub_manage.description: Let linked hubs manage the node: edit its models, change GPU settings, run its fixed actions and follow their jobs. Never its own settings, and never a command of their own. Off when left out.

gpu_data_dir.description: A directory the install scripts of vendors whose drivers are downloaded by hand look for the packages in, under the vendor's name; the working directory when left out.

gpu_sudo.description: Run GPU settings, tool installs and actions that need root with sudo -n when fit does not run as root; sudo must not ask for a password. On when left out.

job_timeout.description: How long a job, an action or an install, may run before it is killed, 10s to 168h. 1h when left out.

refresh_interval.description: How often the node reads its hardware again, 5s to 1h. 30s when left out.

address.description: The peer's host and port, as its listen.address says.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the certificates of the authorities the peer listener's certificate must chain to: the link is made over TLS (wss://), and the certificate must name server_name, or the address's host. Or pin, one of the two.

password.description: The shared password of the dialing role on the peer's listener, deprecated for token: a node dials with the peer's listen.node_password, a proxy with its listen.proxy_password, a hub with its listen.hub_password, or with its listen.password when it has none for the role. Taken in this release, with a warning on the peer's pages; refused in the next.

pin.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the certificate the peer's listener presents, 64 hex digits (colons allowed), as its pages and its log show it: the link is made over TLS (wss://) and only to a listener with exactly that certificate. A peer at an address other than a loopback one needs pin or ca_file.

role.description: The role the peer must announce; a link to a peer of another role is refused. Never the dialing role's own.

server_name.description: The name the peer listener's certificate must have with ca_file, and the TLS server name sent; the address's host when left out.

token.description: The token the peer's listener issued for this role, as fitt1.<id>.<secret>, which the peer's pages, its Admin API module or fit token show once when they make it. Set token or password, not both.

api.description: The API agents on this machine or the LAN call, /v1/chat/completions, /v1/messages, /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent, /api/chat, /v2/chat and the rest; none when left out.

api_keys.description: The keys agents call the API with, each kept as its SHA-256 alone. Its pages make and delete them.

console.description: The proxy's web pages; none when left out.

id.description: The proxy's stable ID, which its peers know it by. Made when left out, and written back here.

limits.description: Bounds on the proxy's links; the defaults when left out.

listen.description: Where the proxy takes links from hubs and nodes; none when left out. Its pages change it.

name.description: The name the proxy shows its peers; the host's name when left out. Its pages change it.

peers.description: The hubs and nodes the proxy dials. Its pages change them.

tokens.description: The tokens the proxy's listener issued, which hubs and nodes link with in place of a password: each its own credential, of no role, kept as a hash, with an optional expiry. The pages, the Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand.

address.description: The host and port the API listens on: a loopback address serves agents on this machine; a LAN address, or an empty host, serves agents on other machines too, and needs cert_file and key_file, so that keys never cross a network in the clear.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the API's certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the API is served over TLS.

first_byte_timeout.description: How long a call may wait for its response to begin. 5m when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate's private key.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest request body a call may carry; one past it gets 413. It is held whole, to read the model it names and to send it again when a route cannot serve it. 32 MiB when left out or 0.

max_conns.description: The most connections the API keeps open at once; one past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. 256 when left out or 0.

max_inflight.description: The most calls the API forwards at once; one past it gets 429. 256 when left out or 0.

timeout.description: The most one call may take, to the end of its response. 30m when left out.

created_at.description: When the key was made, in seconds since 1970.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the key, in hex.

name.description: What the key is for: 1 to 64 characters.

prefix.description: The key's first characters, to tell it by on the pages.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest request body a listener takes, whether it arrives whole or streams through; a larger one gets 413, or, once it has begun to stream, its connection or stream is ended. 16 MiB when left out or 0.

max_conns.description: The most client connections the listeners keep open at once, across all of them; one past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. Takes effect at start, not on a reload. 100000 when left out or 0.

max_header_bytes.description: The largest request header a listener takes; a larger one gets 431. 1 MiB when left out or 0.

max_pending_bytes.description: How many bytes of responses may wait, across every connection, for clients to take them, the backpressure on them all; past it, every connection stops reading until some go. A number of bytes, or a share of the memory fit may use, such as "25%": the machine's, or the container's memory limit where that is lower. Takes effect at start, not on a reload. "50%" when left out or 0; 256 MiB where the memory cannot be read.

max_write_queue_bytes.description: The bytes one connection may have queued for its client before fit closes it, the bound on a peer that stops reading. 32 MiB when left out or 0. Takes effect at start, not on a reload.

write_stall_timeout.description: How long a response may wait for its client to take what it was sent, each time it waits, before the client loses it: its HTTP/1 connection closed, its HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 stream reset. A client that keeps reading, however slowly, is not cut off, and nor is a response that has nothing to send. 30s when left out.

created_at.description: When the token was made, in seconds since 1970.

expires_at.description: When the token expires, in seconds since 1970: it is refused from then on, and the links it holds are closed. Never when left out or 0.

hash.description: The SHA-256 of the key the token's secret derives, in hex: what the listener checks a link's proof with, which cannot be used to link. The token itself is not kept.

id.description: The token's ID, 16 hex digits, the part of the token before its secret; unique among the listener's.

members.description: The members that first linked with the token, which no other token may link as: a tunnel's node/<name> or proxy/<name>, an LLM role's ID. Written by the listener; revoking the token frees them.

name.description: What the token is for, as the pages list it: 1 to 64 characters.

note.description: Anything else about the token, for the pages; up to 1024 bytes.

access.description: The client addresses the listener serves, deciding before the global access: a connection it refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted, or, for HTTP/3 and udp, its datagrams dropped, unless a route or service of the listener sets an access of its own, which then decides first, for its requests or connections. With proxy_protocol the address is the one the header names.

address.description: The host and port to listen on, as in ":8080" or "127.0.0.1:8080".

mptcp.description: Listen the listener's TCP connections with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not; a client without Multipath TCP falls back too. Off by default: a listener is plain TCP. udp listeners and HTTP/3 take none.

name.description: A name unique among the listeners, by which routes refer to this one.

protocols.description: The protocols served: http/1.1, h2c (HTTP/2 in the clear) and, with tls, h2 (HTTP/2 over TLS, chosen through ALPN) and h3 (HTTP/3 over QUIC, on the same port in UDP, announced to HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 clients with Alt-Svc); tcp, raw TCP, whose connections the services that list the listener proxy to their upstreams; socks, a SOCKS5 and SOCKS4 forward proxy, as socks says; or udp alone, whose datagrams a service proxies. A listener that serves more than one of HTTP, tcp and socks tells them apart on its port by what a client sends first: a TLS ClientHello goes to the service whose server_names hold its name, or else, with tls, is served HTTPS, or else goes to the service without server_names; a SOCKS greeting to socks; an HTTP request, in the clear, to HTTP; and whatever else to the service without server_names, or it is closed. A client that waits for the server to speak first is closed after 10s: such a protocol needs a listener of its own. http/1.1 alone when left out, or http/1.1 and h2 with tls.

proxy_protocol.description: Take a PROXY protocol header, of version 1 or 2, at the start of each connection from a trusted address, and serve the connection as from the client it names. For listeners of tcp and of HTTP over TCP; with tls the header comes before TLS. HTTP/3 takes none.

socks.description: Who may use the listener's socks, and where it connects them: needed with socks. It serves CONNECT, without authentication, and refuses BIND and UDP ASSOCIATE.

tls.description: Serve TLS, with these certificates: the listener's HTTP is HTTPS.

format.description: How messages are written, those of every logger loggers does not set one for, as fib writes its own: line, the time, level and message, then the attributes as key=value; text, every part as key=value (logfmt); or json, a JSON object a line. Each carries the logger's name as logger. line when left out. A change takes a restart.

level.description: The least level written, of every logger levels and loggers do not set one for: debug, info, warn or error. info when left out. A change takes effect on reload.

levels.description: The least level of some loggers, by name, over level: server (listeners, loading and reloading configs, shutting down), admin (the Admin API), tls (certificates: ACME, OCSP, certificate files), provider (providers), telemetry (exporting over OTLP), access_log (the access log's dropped lines), plugin (wasm plugins), fastcgi (what FastCGI applications write to their stderr), llm and tunnel (their roles), webrtc (the TURN server) and engine (fib, the network engine, and whatever else writes to Go's log and log/slog). The same as loggers' level, which a logger may not have both of. A change takes effect on reload.

loggers.description: Settings of some loggers of their own, by name (those levels lists), over level, output, format and rotate: engine's to a file of its own, say, or access_log's as json.

output.description: "stdout", "stderr", or the path of a file messages are appended to, of every logger loggers does not set one for. When left out, debug and info messages go to stdout and warn and error ones to stderr. A change takes a restart.

rotate.description: Rotate the file log.output names, and remove old rotated files: the size and interval a file is rotated at, and the age, count and total size past which rotated files are removed. None when left out: the file grows without bound, as before.

time_zone.description: The zone the time of every line is written in, and the zone a file's interval is rotated at: local (the default), utc, or an IANA zone name such as Asia/Shanghai. So 24h turns at local midnight by default, and at UTC midnight with utc. The zone database is embedded, so an IANA name works in a container without zoneinfo. A change takes effect on reload.

format.description: How the logger's messages are written: line, text or json, as the log's format. A change takes a restart.

level.description: The least level the logger writes. A change takes effect on reload.

output.description: "stdout", "stderr", or the path of a file the logger's messages are appended to. A change takes a restart.

rotate.description: Rotate this logger's file, when output names one of its own; the log's rotate is used when the logger writes to the log's output. The settings are the log's rotate's.

expr.description: An expression the request must match, combining matchers with &&, ||, ! and parentheses, as in Host("a.example") && (PathPrefix("/api/") || Method("POST")). Its matchers are Host, Path, PathPrefix, PathRegexp, Method, Header(name, value...), Query(key, value...) and RemoteIP, whose arguments are strings quoted as in Go. It counts as one matcher in the order of routes, and its hosts and paths do not make a route more specific: give it a priority.

header.description: Headers the request must have, each with one of the values listed as the value of one of its fields, or with any value when none are listed. Names ignore case; values do not.

host.description: Host names, exact, or with a leading "*." wildcard, which stands for one label, or a leading "**." wildcard, which stands for one label or more, as the Gateway API's wildcards do.

method.description: Methods, as in "GET"; compared as written, since methods are case-sensitive.

path.description: Paths, exact or ending in "*" to match a prefix.

path_regexp.description: Regular expressions in Go's syntax, matched against the path anywhere in it unless anchored with ^ and $.

query.description: Query parameters the request must have, each with one of the values listed, or with any value when none are listed; compared once unescaped.

remote_ip.description: IP addresses and CIDR prefixes, as in "10.0.0.0/8", the client's address must be in: the address of the connection, not of X-Forwarded-For.

keys.description: A keyring of signing keys, each a name and its secret or secret_file, in place of secret or secret_file: a token is signed with one key and checked against every key, so rotating one key, as the handler media_tokens does, refuses only the tokens that key signed and the others stay good. One of the two: keys, or secret/secret_file. None when left out.

name.description: The policy's name, which the auth param of whip, whep and webrtc_proxy, and the media roles, refer to it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'.

public.description: The actions anyone may take without credentials, as ["play"] for streams anyone may watch and only some may publish. None when left out: every request needs credentials.

secret.description: The key, at least 16 bytes, that tokens fit issues are signed with (HMAC-SHA256): fit media-token's and the media pages' logins. Tokens are good for this policy alone, until their expiry. When left out, a random key of the process's signs the pages' logins, which a restart forgets; fit media-token needs it. Or secret_file, one of the two, or keys.

secret_file.description: A file holding the secret tokens are signed with, read each time the config is applied: the handler media_tokens rotates it, and every token signed before is refused. At least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside. Or secret, one of the two, or keys. None when left out: a random key of the process's signs, which a restart forgets.

token_ttl.description: How long a token fit issues is good for, unless fit media-token's -ttl says otherwise. 12h when left out.

tokens.description: Static bearer tokens, each with the streams it may publish and play: sent as Authorization: Bearer, a token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie.

url_signing.description: Turns on playback URLs that expire: URLs signed for one viewer and one resource (an item of vod, a stream of hls or httpflv) with the policy's secret or a key of its keys, as media_tokens' /urls issues them, and checked by those handlers on every playlist, segment and subtitle, at once and without a callback. Needs secret, secret_file or keys. Off when left out.

users.description: Users with a password, each with the streams they may publish and play: sent as Authorization: Basic, as user and pass query parameters where a protocol has no header (RTMP, SRT), or RTSP's Digest. They also log in to fit's media pages, which hand out tokens signed with secret.

key.description: The key's name: 1 to 64 letters, digits, '_', '.', '~' and '-', which a media_tokens request names to sign with it, and a revoke to rotate it.

secret.description: The key's secret, at least 16 bytes. Or secret_file, one of the two.

secret_file.description: A file holding the key's secret, read each time the config is applied; the handler media_tokens rotates this file to refuse just the tokens this key signed. At least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside. Or secret, one of the two.

exclude.description: Files and directories left out, by pattern, as files writes them, as trailers or **/extras/**; a directory left out is not walked. None when left out.

file_queue.description: The most jobs that wait for the file pool; one more is refused, as a request answered 503. 4096 when left out or 0.

file_timeout.description: How long a job may wait for the file pool before it is given up, as a request answered 503. 10s when left out.

file_workers.description: The goroutines of the library's file pool, which probe, read sample tables and read the files' bytes, so that no fib worker waits on the disk: all the disk is asked to do at once. 4 a CPU, and at least 16, when left out or 0.

files.description: The files looked at, by pattern: a pattern without '/' matches a file's name, as *.mp4, and one with '/' its path under the root, as films/**/*.mp4, where * matches within a name and ** any run of directories. Every file when left out; names starting with '.' are never looked at.

follow_symlinks.description: Follow symbolic links that lead out of the library's roots. A link that stays within its root is followed either way; one that leads out is refused, and reported, when left out or false.

max_catalog_bytes.description: The most memory the catalog takes, as reckoned from its items' paths, titles, tracks and codec configurations; past it the rest of the items are left out, and the scan says so. 64 MiB when left out or 0.

max_files.description: The most files and directories a scan looks at, across the roots; past it the scan stops there, and says so. 200000 when left out or 0.

max_items.description: The most items the catalog holds; past it the rest are left out, and the scan says so. 20000 when left out or 0.

max_probes.description: The most files probed at once on the library's file pool, so that a scan leaves the pool's other workers to the files being served. 4 when left out or 0.

max_sidecar_bytes.description: The largest sidecar, <name>.json, read; a larger one is reported and left out. At most 1 MiB. 64 KiB when left out or 0.

max_subtitle_bytes.description: The largest subtitle file served, .vtt or .srt turned into WebVTT; a larger one is listed with its error and not served. 2 MiB when left out or 0.

max_table_bytes.description: The most memory the sample tables read from the files take, kept for the files being served; past it the least recently used are dropped, and a table larger than all of it is refused. 128 MiB when left out or 0.

max_upload_bytes.description: The largest file uploaded; a larger one is refused 413 before any of it is written. 32 GiB when left out or 0.

max_uploads.description: The most uploads under way at once, begun and not yet whole; one more is refused 429 until one ends, or is cancelled, or expires. 4 when left out or 0.

min_free_bytes.description: The disk space left free beside the uploads under way: an upload whose bytes, with those of the others still to come, would leave less free on upload_dir's disk is refused 507 before any of it is written. 1 GiB when left out or 0.

name.description: The library's name, which handlers and the Admin API's /media/library/<name> refer to it by. Letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-'.

roots.description: The directories whose files the library holds, scanned with their subdirectories; an item's id is its path under its root. A root may not lie inside another. A root missing when scanned is reported, and the others are scanned.

scan_interval.description: How often the roots are scanned again, at least 10s; a scan also runs when the library is made, when the config changes its roots, patterns or bounds, and on the Admin API's POST /media/library/<name>/rescan. A file whose size and time are unchanged is not probed again. 10m when left out.

secret.description: The secret, at least 16 bytes, the AES-128 keys of encrypted HLS are derived from: a key for each item of vod with encrypt, and for each channel with encrypt, rotated every key_rotation segments. Changing it changes every key, so that segments encrypted before, kept by a CDN, no longer play: purge them. Or secret_file, one of the two. None when left out: nothing of the library can be encrypted.

secret_file.description: A file holding the secret the AES-128 keys of encrypted HLS are derived from, read each time the config is applied. At least 16 bytes, its line breaks at the end aside. Or secret, one of the two. None when left out.

upload_dir.description: A directory inside one of the roots, or a root itself, that files uploaded from the workbench, or the Admin API's /media/library/<name>/uploads, are written into: in pieces, resumable after a cut connection, to a temporary file named .fit-upload-*, renamed into place once whole and probed by the scan that follows. Made when missing. None when left out: no uploads; the files of the library are still renamed, moved and deleted from the workbench.

upload_expiry.description: How long an upload not written to is kept before it is given up and its temporary file removed, at the next scan; at least 1m. An upload is kept across restarts until then. 24h when left out.

name.description: What the token is called in logs, which never show the token itself: token:<name>, or token when left out.

play.description: The streams the token may play, as publish lists them. None when left out.

publish.description: The streams the token may publish, by name or path, with * matching any run of characters, '/' among them, as live/* or room1-*. None when left out.

token.description: The token, at least 16 characters. Or token_sha256, one of the two.

token_sha256.description: Instead of the token, its SHA-256 in hex, so that the config does not hold it, as sha256sum prints it for the token alone, without a newline: printf %s "$TOKEN" | sha256sum.

name.description: The user's name; it may not contain a colon or a control character.

password.description: The user's password. A user with one can also log in with RTSP's Digest, which needs the password itself. Or password_hash, one of the two.

password_hash.description: Instead of the password, its bcrypt hash, as fit hash-password makes it: Basic and the query's user and pass only, checked off fib's workers. A password once found right is remembered, as a keyed SHA-256, so that the next check is at once.

play.description: The streams the user may play. None when left out.

publish.description: The streams the user may publish, as a token's publish lists them. None when left out.

interval.description: How often the metrics are exported. 30s when left out.

ask.description: A URL fit asks, with the name in the query as domain=<name>, whether a name may have a certificate: an answer of 2xx allows it, and any other refuses it. Refusals are remembered for a minute. At most 8 asks are under way at once, and 5 a second on average, 20 at once, however they are answered; a handshake past them fails without asking.

idle_timeout.description: How long a name taken on demand is kept, and renewed, with no handshake asking for it; then it is dropped and no longer counts against max_names, and its certificate stays in the storage for the next handshake that asks for it, which the ask URL must allow again. 168h, a week, when left out.

interval.description: The interval rate counts over. 1m when left out.

max_names.description: How many names may have certificates obtained on demand, in all; past it, a handshake for another fails. 1000 when left out or 0.

rate.description: How many certificates may be obtained every interval; a handshake past it fails. 10 when left out or 0.

timeout.description: How long a handshake waits for its name's certificate, as long as fib's handshake timeout by default. 10s when left out.

block_profile_rate.description: Sample goroutines blocking on channels, selects and locks for the block profile: one event per this many nanoseconds spent blocked, on average, 1 for every one. 0, none, when left out; set it only while looking, since it costs every blocking event.

max_duration.description: The longest a profile's seconds may ask for: a CPU profile or a trace samples for that long, and a delta profile waits that long, holding its connection to the Admin API all the while; a request for longer is refused with 400. 1m when left out.

mutex_profile_fraction.description: Sample one in this many contended mutexes for the mutex profile, 1 for every one. 0, none, when left out.

consul.description: Routes, upstreams and services from the tags of the services in a Consul catalog, sending to their instances whose health checks pass.

consul_kv.description: Listeners, routes, upstreams and services from the keys under a prefix in Consul's KV store, each holding a JSON object of them.

docker.description: Routes, upstreams and services from the labels of running Docker containers.

etcd.description: Listeners, routes, upstreams and services from the keys under a prefix in etcd, each holding a JSON object of them.

kubernetes.description: Listeners, routes, services and upstreams from a Kubernetes cluster's Gateway API resources: the Gateways of the GatewayClasses whose controllerName is fit's, and their HTTPRoutes, GRPCRoutes, TLSRoutes, TCPRoutes and UDPRoutes, whose status fit writes back.

name.description: The name the provider goes by in the Admin API's /config/effective and in logs: lower-case letters, digits, '_', '.' and '-', unique among the providers. Its kind, as docker, when left out.

trusted.description: The addresses and CIDR ranges of the proxies that send the header, as "10.0.0.0/8": a connection from one of them must begin with a header, within 10s, or it is closed, and one from elsewhere is served as it is, with no header.

address.description: The server's host and port. 127.0.0.1:6379 when left out.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs the server's certificate is verified with, over TLS; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over TLS; with key_file.

db.description: The database selected. 0 when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

password_file.description: A file holding the password to authenticate with, read at each connection; none when left out.

username.description: The ACL user to authenticate as, with password_file; the default user when left out.

address.description: The host and port the pages listen on. A host that is not a loopback address needs cert_file and key_file, so that passwords never cross a network in the clear.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the pages' certificate, followed by any intermediates; with key_file, the pages are served over TLS.

key_file.description: A PEM file with the certificate's private key.

max_conns.description: The most connections the pages keep open at once, a quarter of them kept for those with a login. When they are taken, a new connection closes the oldest of those without one, of the client holding the most, and is closed as it is accepted only when every one has a login; one past a client's share, a quarter of them, is closed too, but for loopback clients. 32 when left out or 0.

max_sessions.description: The most logins kept at once; one more ends the oldest. 64 when left out or 0.

mptcp.description: Listen the pages with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default.

session_lifetime.description: How long a login lasts at most, however busy. 12h when left out.

session_timeout.description: How long a login lasts without a request. 30m when left out.

users.description: Who may log in: at least one user.

compress.description: Gzip a file when it is rotated. On when left out.

interval.description: How long a file is written before it is rotated, at the next period boundary of the log's time_zone: 24h turns at midnight, 1h on the hour; a fraction of a second, or a period over 24h that is not a whole number of days, is refused. Off when left out.

max_age.description: How long a rotated file is kept after it was last written: 720h (30 days) when left out; 0 keeps it until a count or size limit removes it.

max_bytes.description: How large a file may grow before it is rotated: a write that would take it past this starts a new file. 1 GiB when left out; 0 does not rotate by size.

max_files.description: The most rotated files kept, newest first; 0 or left out has no count limit.

max_total_bytes.description: The most the rotated files may total, the oldest removed until they fit. 1 GiB when left out; 0 does not limit the total.

access.description: The client addresses the route serves, deciding before its listener's access and the global one: a request it refuses is answered 403. The address is the connection's, or the one its PROXY header names, not X-Forwarded-For's.

listeners.description: The names of the listeners the route serves; every listener when left out.

match.description: What a request must match; every request when left out.

middleware.description: Middleware a request passes through, in order, before the handler.

name.description: A name unique among the routes, for logs and metrics.

priority.description: Routes with a higher priority are picked first; among equal ones, the most specific host, then path, then the one with the most other matchers set (method, header, query, remote_ip, path_regexp, expr), then the one written first.

access.description: The client addresses the service takes, deciding before its listener's access and the global one: a connection it refuses is closed, once its PROXY header and ClientHello are read when the listener needs them, and the datagrams of a udp session it refuses are dropped.

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection or a udp session may carry nothing either way before both sides are closed; 10m for a connection and 1m for a udp session when left out.

listeners.description: The names of the listeners whose connections the service takes: those that serve tcp, alone or beside other protocols, and udp listeners, each one service's. A udp listener's session is a client's address: the datagrams it sends go to one upstream address, from a socket of the session's own, and what comes back to that socket goes to the client.

max_conns.description: The most connections and udp sessions the service proxies at once; a connection past it is closed as soon as it is accepted, and the datagrams of a session past it are dropped. 10000 when left out or 0.

name.description: A name unique among the services.

proxy_protocol.description: Send each upstream connection a PROXY protocol header of this version (v1, text, or v2, binary) first, naming the client's address and the one it connected to. For tcp listeners.

server_names.description: The server names (SNI) of the TLS connections the service takes from its tcp listeners, which it proxies as they are, without terminating their TLS; "*.example.com" takes the names one label below example.com. A tcp listener may then be listed by several services: a connection goes to the one whose names hold the name its ClientHello asks for, or else to the listener's service without server_names, if it has one, as one that is not TLS or asks for no name does; otherwise it is closed. The ClientHello must come within 10s.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream connections go to: one of its addresses, picked by its load_balancing (ip_hash by the client's address; header, cookie and URI hashes, which a connection has none of, in turn), out of rotation for its max_fails and health checks as for HTTP, dialed within its connect_timeout. A connect that fails is tried on the next address picked, up to three addresses. Its protocol and HTTP settings are not used.

consul.description: Keep them in Consul's KV store, with locks held by sessions.

etcd.description: Keep them in etcd, through its v3 JSON gateway, with locks held by leases.

lock_ttl.description: How long a lock outlives an instance that stopped holding it without giving it back; its holder renews it every third of that. At least 10s; 30s when left out.

prefix.description: What the keys kept start with, as fit/certificates/<CA>/<name>.pem; instances that share certificates share it. fit/ when left out.

redis.description: Keep them in Redis, a standalone server or a primary (not Redis Cluster), with locks of SET NX and an expiry.

request_timeout.description: How long each request to the store may take, connecting included. 10s when left out.
