max_age.description: How long the client keeps the cookie, as its Max-Age; until the browser closes when left out.

name.description: The cookie's name; fit_sticky when left out.

path.description: The cookie's Path; / when left out.

secure.description: Mark the cookie Secure, so that it is sent only over HTTPS. It is always HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.

password.description: The password the store is encrypted with. Written here, it protects a store copied away from this file, not one read beside it; password_file or password_env keep it out of the file.

password_env.description: An environment variable holding the password.

password_file.description: A file holding the password, its surrounding spaces trimmed.

path.description: The store's file, made 0600 when it is written. fit stops at start if it exists and does not open with the password.

encrypt.description: Encrypts the channel's HLS segments with AES-128 (METHOD=AES-128), fMP4 and MPEG-TS alike, under a key derived from the library's secret, which the hls handler serves only to a request its auth lets play the channel; so that segments copied, as a CDN keeps them, do not play without it. Needs the library's secret or secret_file. Low-Latency HLS parts are encrypted too, each on its own. The other egresses play the channel as before, under their auth. Off when left out.

items.description: The IDs of the library's items the channel plays, in this order unless order is shuffle, and again from the first when loop is on; between the schedule's slots too. An item the library does not hold, or cannot serve, is skipped. At most 10000.

key_rotation.description: With encrypt, how many segments one key encrypts before the next takes over, so that a key handed out opens a few segments only. 10 when left out or 0.

library.description: The media_library the channel's items are of.

loop.description: Play items again from the first once the last has played. With loop off, the channel goes quiet after the last, staying published, until its next slot, or until the Admin API stops and starts it, which plays the list again from the first. On when left out.

max_buffer_bytes.description: The most bytes read ahead and not yet sent, whatever read_ahead says, at least 1 MiB; a sample larger than it ends its item. 16 MiB when left out or 0.

name.description: The stream the channel publishes into the hub, as tv/films: every egress of the streaming role plays it by that path, under its auth, as rtmp://host/tv/films or /hls/tv/films/index.m3u8. Parts of letters, digits, '.', '_', '~' and '-', split at '/'. A channel renamed is another channel: the old one ends.

order.description: The order items are played in: sequence, as listed, or shuffle, every item once in a random order each time round. sequence when left out.

push.description: Outside servers the channel is relayed to, as streaming's push names them, their stream being the channel's.

read_ahead.description: How much of the items is read ahead of what is sent, on the library's file pool, so that a slow disk does not stall the channel and the next item follows the last without a gap. 500ms to 1m. 3s when left out.

rendition.description: The rendition played of each item, by its name, as 720p; one an item lacks plays its best instead. The rendition with the most pixels, the highest bit rate among equals, when left out.

schedule.description: Items started at set times, in time_zone, cutting what plays: daily, on days of the week, or once. A slot whose time has passed while its item would still be playing, when the channel starts, is joined where it would be. Between slots the channel plays items, or goes quiet without them. At most 1000.

time_zone.description: The IANA time zone the schedule's times are in, as Asia/Shanghai or Local for the host's. UTC when left out.

connect_timeout.description: How long connecting may take, the RTMP handshake and publish or the SRT handshake. 10s when left out.

name.description: The target's name in the Admin API and the metrics, unique among the push targets. The stream's name and the target's place among the stream's when left out, as tv/films#1.

retry_max.description: The longest a retry waits. 30s when left out.

retry_min.description: How long the first retry waits, after a target refuses, drops or cannot be reached, or the stream is not published; each retry waits twice the last, up to retry_max, and a push that has stayed up retry_max starts again from retry_min. 1s when left out.

stream.description: The stream of the hub relayed, as live/cam or a channel's name. Required in streaming's push; a channel's push targets relay the channel.

url.description: Where the stream is sent: rtmp://host[:port]/app/stream, or rtmps://, publishing to an RTMP server as a CDN's ingest takes it; or srt://host:port?streamid=...&passphrase=...&latency=ms, calling an SRT listener with MPEG-TS. The URL is a secret, its stream key with it: the Admin API and the logs show its scheme, host and app alone.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a publish and a play must satisfy, by the stream's path, app/stream: credentials go in the query of the stream name or the app, as rtmp://host/live/cam?token=T or ?user=U&pass=P. A refusal is answered with NetStream.Publish.Unauthorized or NetStream.Play.Failed and the connection closed. Everyone may publish and play when left out. A change applies to the next publish and play.

handshake_timeout.description: How long a client may take from connecting to publishing or playing. 10s when left out.

idle_timeout.description: How long a publisher may send nothing, and a player's output not move, before its connection is closed. 30s when left out.

listen.description: The TCP address RTMP clients connect to, as in ":1935". A change of any field but auth starts the listener again, closing its connections.

max_conns.description: The most connections at once; one more is closed as it opens. 1024 when left out or 0.

max_message_bytes.description: The largest RTMP message a client may send, a video frame among them; a larger one closes its connection. 8 MiB when left out or 0.

mptcp.description: Listen the RTMP connections with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default.

play_wait.description: How long a player may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, or for the next one after its publisher leaves. A play of a stream without a publisher fails at once when left out.

auth.description: The media_auth policy RTSP requests must satisfy, by the stream's path: ANNOUNCE publish and DESCRIBE play on the stream their URL names, RECORD publish and PLAY play on the stream of the connection's session (one whose URL names another stream is refused with 455), and a SETUP play on its stream, or once a session is set up, play or publish on the session's. Credentials are a user with a plaintext password by Digest, a user by Basic when auth_methods offers it, or a token in the URL's query, as rtsp://host/live/cam?token=T. A refusal is 401 with the challenges, or 403. Everyone may publish and play when left out. A change applies to the next request.

auth_methods.description: The schemes a 401 offers for users: digest, which needs a user's plaintext password, and basic, which sends the password in the clear and is the only one a password_hash user can use. ["digest"] when left out.

idle_timeout.description: How long a connection without a session may go without a request before it is closed. 60s when left out.

listen.description: The TCP address RTSP clients connect to, as in ":8554". RTP goes interleaved on the same connection (RTP/AVP/TCP); a SETUP asking for UDP is answered 461, which ffmpeg and most players then retry over TCP. A change of any field but auth starts the listener again, closing its connections.

max_conns.description: The most connections at once; one more is closed as it opens. 1024 when left out or 0.

mptcp.description: Listen the RTSP connections with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default.

play_wait.description: How long a player may outlive its stream's publisher, waiting for the next one. A player ends with its publisher when left out.

realm.description: The realm of the challenges, which Digest's response is computed with. fit when left out.

session_timeout.description: How long a session may go without a request, RTCP or, while recording, RTP before it and its connection end; clients are told so in the Session header and send keep-alives. 60s when left out.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a caller must satisfy, publish for m=publish and play otherwise, by the stream ID's resource: a token as s= (#!::r=live/cam,m=publish,s=T), a user and password as u= and s=, or token, or user and pass, in the resource's query (live/cam?token=T). A refusal rejects the handshake with 1401 (unauthorized) or 1403 (forbidden). Everyone may publish and play when left out. A change applies to the next caller.

latency.description: The receive latency asked for, the time a packet may take to be sent again when lost; the caller's wins when larger. 120ms when left out.

listen.description: The UDP address SRT callers reach, as in ":8890". A change of any field but auth starts the listener again, ending its sessions.

max_conns.description: The most sessions at once; one more caller is rejected with 1402. 1024 when left out or 0.

passphrase.description: Encrypt every session with this passphrase, 10 to 79 characters, which callers must have too (pbkeylen 16). Unencrypted when left out.

peer_idle_timeout.description: How long a peer may send nothing, keep-alives included, before its session ends. 5s when left out.

play_wait.description: How long a player may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, or for the next one after its publisher leaves. A caller playing a stream without a publisher is rejected with 1404 when left out.

connect_timeout.description: How long a session may take from its answer to a connected PeerConnection before it is ended; once connected, ICE consent bounds it. 15s when left out.

ice_servers.description: STUN and TURN servers the peers are told of in Link headers (RFC 9725), for their side of ICE; fit's is an ICE lite agent on its own address.

listen.description: The UDP address every peer's media reaches fit at, one port all the role's PeerConnections share, as in ":8188"; not webrtc.media's. A wildcard host advertises every interface's address that is up, unless public_ips is set. A change of any field starts it again, ending its sessions.

max_offer_bytes.description: The largest offer taken; a larger one is answered 400. At most 64 KiB. 32 KiB when left out or 0.

max_sessions.description: The most WHIP and WHEP sessions at once; one more offer is answered 503. 256 when left out or 0.

play_wait.description: How long a WHEP offer may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, its request held, before it is answered 404. Answered 404 at once when left out.

public_ips.description: The addresses peers are told to reach the port at instead of the interfaces' own, as behind a 1:1 NAT.

access.description: The client addresses the rtmp, rtsp, srt and webrtc listeners serve, deciding before the global access: a connection it refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted, and the datagrams of an srt caller or webrtc peer it refuses are dropped. A change applies to the next connection and peer, without starting a listener again; those connected are kept.

channels.description: Channels: items of a media_library played into the hub as live streams, in order, shuffled, looped or on a schedule, paced by their timestamps, which run on from one item to the next; every egress plays them under its auth. A reload changes a channel in place, from its next item. At most 256. None when left out.

gop_cache_bytes.description: The bytes each stream keeps of its latest group of pictures, from its last key frame on, so that a new player starts at once with a picture; a group that outgrows it is dropped and caching starts again at the next key frame. 8 MiB when left out or 0.

max_players.description: The most players of one stream at once, over every protocol, HLS counting once a stream and format; one more is refused. Each packet a publisher sends is handed to every player on the worker that received it. 256 when left out or 0.

max_streams.description: The most streams at once, each a path with a publisher or players waiting for one; one more publisher is refused. 64 when left out or 0. A change of max_streams, max_players or gop_cache_bytes starts the hub again, ending every stream and connection.

push.description: Outside RTMP or SRT servers, as a CDN's ingest, that streams of the hub are relayed to, each reconnected with backoff when it drops; a channel's own push lists its own. A reload keeps a target whose stream and url are unchanged connected. At most 256 in all. None when left out.

rtmp.description: Take and play streams over RTMP, as rtmp://host/app/stream: OBS and ffmpeg publish, players play. None when left out.

rtsp.description: Take and play streams over RTSP 1.0 with interleaved RTP (RTP/AVP/TCP), as rtsp://host/app/stream. None when left out.

srt.description: Take and play streams over SRT, MPEG-TS on UDP, the stream named by the caller's stream ID. None when left out.

webrtc.description: The UDP port the PeerConnections of the stream_whip and stream_whep handlers share, which publish into the hub with WHIP and play from it with WHEP. Routes with those handlers answer 503 without it. None when left out.

acme.description: Host names to obtain certificates for with ACME, as the top-level acme says, through its challenges: the CA must reach fit at each name on port 80, where any listener of fit's in the clear answers HTTP-01, or on port 443, where this listener answers TLS-ALPN-01. A client asking for one of these names is given its certificate once there is one; until then, and for other names, the certificates from files.

certificates.description: Certificates from files. A client is given the first whose names match the one it asks for, or the first of all when none does or it asks for none.

client_auth.description: Ask clients for certificates and verify them (mutual TLS).

on_demand.description: Obtain a certificate during the handshake for a name a client asks for that neither the files nor acme have, as the top-level acme.on_demand allows; needs it.

access.description: The client addresses the server serves on listen, listen_tcp and listen_tls, deciding before the global access: a connection it refuses is closed as soon as it is accepted, and the datagrams of a UDP client it refuses are dropped. Peers are not clients: allowed_peers and denied_peers decide those. A change applies to the next client, without starting a new server; the allocations held are kept.

allowed_peers.description: The addresses and prefixes, as in "10.1.0.0/16", peers may be at even when denied_peers or the default denial cover them: loopback, private, link-local and other internal ranges are denied unless listed here, so that the relay cannot reach into the network it runs in. An address with a port, as in "10.0.0.5:8189", allows that port alone, which is how a peer on relay_ip itself, such as webrtc.media, is reached.

default_lifetime.description: The lifetime of an allocation whose client asks for less, or for none; clients refresh it before it ends. 10m when left out. Applies to the next allocation or refresh.

denied_peers.description: Addresses and prefixes peers may not be at, beyond the internal ranges denied by default; an address with a port denies that port alone.

listen.description: The UDP addresses clients reach the server at, as in ":3478", the port TURN's turn: URIs default to. A change of listen, listen_tcp or listen_tls starts a new server and drains the old one.

listen_tcp.description: TCP addresses clients reach the server at, as in ":3478", for clients on networks that block UDP: turn:host:3478?transport=tcp. Their allocations relay UDP, and end when their connection closes.

listen_tls.description: TLS addresses clients reach the server at, as in ":5349" or ":443", with tls's certificates, for clients that only TLS gets through for: turns:host:5349?transport=tcp. As listen_tcp otherwise.

max_allocations.description: The most allocations held at once; one more is refused with 508. Each holds a relayed socket on every event loop. 1024 when left out or 0. A change applies to the next allocation; those held past a lowered one are kept until they end.

max_allocations_per_user.description: The most allocations of one username; one more is refused with 486. 16 when left out or 0. Applies to the next allocation.

max_channels.description: The most channels one allocation binds; one more is refused with 508. 64 when left out or 0. Applies to the next request.

max_lifetime.description: The longest lifetime a client may ask for. 1h when left out. Applies to the next allocation or refresh.

max_permissions.description: The most permissions, peer addresses, one allocation holds; one more is refused with 508. A channel's peer counts. 64 when left out or 0. Applies to the next request.

max_stream_message.description: The largest message a TCP or TLS client may send, and so what its connection buffers of one not yet whole; a connection whose next message claims more is closed. At least 2048. 8 KiB when left out or 0. A change starts a new server.

mptcp.description: Listen listen_tcp and listen_tls with Multipath TCP where the kernel offers it (Linux 5.6+, net.mptcp.enabled), falling back to plain TCP where it does not. Off by default; listen's UDP sockets have none. A change of it starts a new server and drains the old one.

nonce_lifetime.description: How long a nonce is good for; a request with an older one is answered 438 with a fresh one. 10m when left out. Applies to the next nonce.

nonce_secret.description: The key nonces are made with; a random one when left out. Servers behind one load balancer, which may each see a client's requests, share one. A change starts a new server.

port_max.description: The highest port of the relayed sockets; with port_min.

port_min.description: The lowest port of the relayed sockets, as a firewall that opens a range expects; with port_max. Ports the kernel picks when both are left out. A change starts a new server.

public_ip.description: The address clients are told for their relayed sockets instead of relay_ip, for a server behind a 1:1 NAT that maps it to relay_ip. Of relay_ip's family. A change starts a new server.

realm.description: The realm of the credentials, sent in every challenge: clients derive their key from their name, the realm and their password. A change starts a new server, ending the allocations of the old one when they share an address and draining it otherwise.

relay_ip.description: The address the relayed sockets bind to, one of the host's, not a wildcard; clients are told it, unless public_ip is set. Its family is every allocation's. Peers on it, and on public_ip, are relayed to on the ports of the server's own relayed addresses alone, and on those allowed_peers lists with their port. A change starts a new server.

secret.description: The shared secret of time-limited credentials, as coturn's static-auth-secret (use-auth-secret) has it: a username "<expiry in Unix seconds>:<anything>" whose password is the base64 of HMAC-SHA1(secret, username), valid until the expiry. A web service that knows the secret hands them out.

stream_idle_timeout.description: How long a TCP or TLS client's connection may stay open without an allocation, before its first Allocate or after its allocation ended, before it is closed. 30s when left out. A change starts a new server.

tls.description: The certificates of listen_tls, from files, as a listener's tls.certificates has them, and watched as theirs are: a change applies to the next handshake.

user_bandwidth.description: The most bytes a second relayed for one username each way, to peers and from them, with a second's worth of burst; datagrams past it are dropped. 2 MiB when left out or 0.

users.description: The users with fixed credentials. With secret, or alone; at least one of the two.

certificates.description: Certificates from files. A client is given the first whose names match the one it asks for, or the first of all when none does or it asks for none.

key.description: Instead of the password, the long-term key it derives, as coturn's turnadmin -k prints it: MD5(name ":" realm ":" password) in hex, optionally after 0x, so that the password is not kept.

name.description: The username.

ca_file.description: A PEM file with the CAs the receiver's certificate is verified with, over https; the system's when left out.

cert_file.description: A PEM file with the client certificate sent over https; with key_file.

endpoint.description: The OTLP/HTTP receiver: http:// or https:// and a host and port, as of an OpenTelemetry Collector; traces go to its /v1/traces and metrics to /v1/metrics, as JSON. http://127.0.0.1:4318 when left out.

headers_file.description: A file of header fields sent with each export, one "Name: value" a line, as an API key a receiver asks for; read when fit starts. None when left out.

key_file.description: A PEM file with cert_file's private key.

metrics.description: Export the metrics the Admin API's /metrics serves, requests counted included, every interval. No metrics over OTLP when left out.

service_name.description: The service.name of the resource traces and metrics are about. fit when left out.

timeout.description: How long an export may take, connecting included; a batch not sent by then is dropped and counted. 10s when left out.

traces.description: Trace requests: a server span for each one sampled, and its context sent on to upstreams in traceparent. No traces when left out.

interval.description: How often spans are exported, and sooner when 256 KiB of them wait. 5s when left out.

max_queue_bytes.description: The most bytes of spans waiting to be exported, besides the batch being sent; spans past it are dropped and counted. 4 MiB when left out or 0.

sample_ratio.description: The share of requests traced among those whose caller did not decide: from 0 to 1. A request whose traceparent says its caller sampled it is always traced, and one that says it did not is never. 0, only those a caller sampled, when left out.

hub.description: Run a hub: nodes and proxies link to it, and it joins a proxy's tunnels to a node's.

node.description: Run a node: it links to hubs and opens the tunnels they ask for to the services it exposes.

proxy.description: Run a proxy: local ports and web proxies forwarded through a hub to the services of a node.

address.description: The host and port the WebSocket listens on; it answers on any path.

max_conns.description: The most WebSockets open at once; one past it is closed as soon as it opens. A WebSocket that has not proven the password, with a message it seals, is closed after 10s, and one IP address may have a quarter of them open that have not. 32 when left out or 0.

password.description: The password the WebSocket's messages are encrypted with, which a proxy's web_proxy needs. The hub's password when left out.

address.description: The hub's address: tls://host:port for TCP over TLS, wss://host:port/path for a WebSocket over TLS, quic://host:port for QUIC; or, only to a loopback host or with body_password, host:port or tcp://host:port for TCP and ws://host:port/path for a WebSocket in the clear. An address has no query, fragment or user ('?', '#', '@'): pin and ca_file say how the hub's certificate is checked.

disabled.description: Leave the endpoint out of the dials, keeping it for later.

hub.description: The name of the hub the tunnels go through. When left out, they are spread over every hub that has the node, more of them through the faster ones.

listen.description: The local host and port the forward listens on.

node.description: The node whose service the tunnels go to.

service.description: The node's service the tunnels go to.

allow_proxy_services.description: Let registered proxies set nodes' services through the hub, as a proxy's pages do; a node takes them only with its allow_hub_services. Every proxy that has the password could then do it. Off when left out: only the hub's own pages ask nodes to change their services.

body_password.description: When set, the body of every frame on the links is encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and nodes and proxies need the same one: each frame is authenticated, so a tcp or ws listener on an address that is not a loopback one is allowed only with it. A link registered with a token derives its keys from the token and this, by HKDF; one with the password, from the password's PBKDF2. It applies to the links that open after it changes.

call_timeout.description: How long a node may take to answer the hub: to open a tunnel, or to list or set its services. 15s when left out.

console.description: The hub's web pages; none when left out.

console_socket.description: An encrypted WebSocket that carries the hub's console pages to the web_proxies of proxies that cannot reach them otherwise. Needs console. None when left out.

listeners.description: Where nodes and proxies link to the hub, each over its protocol. A tcp or ws listener on an address that is not a loopback one needs body_password: use tls, wss or quic there. None when left out: the console's pages add them.

max_links.description: The most links the hub keeps open at once, registered or not; one past it is closed as soon as it opens. 1024 when left out or 0.

max_links_per_peer.description: The most links one node or proxy may register, from however many processes of the same name. 128 when left out or 0.

max_peers.description: The most nodes and proxies registered at once. 1024 when left out or 0.

max_tunnels.description: The most tunnels the hub passes at once; a proxy's request for one more is refused. 16384 when left out or 0.

max_unregistered.description: The most links open at once that have not registered yet, which anyone who reaches a listener can open; one past it is closed as soon as it opens, so that they cannot take every link from the nodes and proxies that register. 256 when left out or 0.

max_unregistered_per_ip.description: The most links from one IP address open at once that have not registered yet; one past it is closed as soon as it opens, and its node or proxy links again after its retry_interval. 32 when left out or 0.

name.description: The name the hub tells the nodes and proxies that register. The host's name when left out.

password.description: The password every node and proxy may register with, which they prove they know without sending it: deprecated for tokens, which give each member a credential of its own. Still taken in this release, with a warning on the pages while a member uses it; refused in the next. Without it, only tokens register.

quic.description: The hub's certificate, which its tls, wss and quic listeners present unless they have cert_file, and the connections of the quic listeners. The hub makes a self-signed certificate and writes it here when a listener needs one and none is set.

register_timeout.description: How long a link may take to register once it is open; it is closed past it. 10s when left out.

tokens.description: The tokens the hub issued, which nodes and proxies register with in place of the password: each its own credential, kept as a hash, with an optional expiry. The hub's pages, its Admin API module and fit token make, list, change and revoke them; not written by hand.

cert.description: The PEM certificate the tls, wss and quic listeners without cert_file present, which nodes and proxies pin by its SHA-256 fingerprint; with key. When a listener needs one and none is set, the hub makes a self-signed one and keeps it: here, with admin.store, or else in a file beside the config, 0600, as fit.tunnel.hub.pem beside fit.json; so that it outlives a restart, and the pins of it stay good.

handshake_timeout.description: How long a QUIC handshake may take. 10s when left out.

idle_timeout.description: How long a QUIC connection may hear nothing from its peer before it is closed. 30s when left out.

keep_alive.description: How often a quiet QUIC connection is pinged, so that it neither idles out nor loses its NAT mapping. 10s when left out.

key.description: The PEM private key of cert.

max_handshakes.description: The most QUIC handshakes under way at once; a new connection past it is dropped, and its proxy tries again. Past half of them, a client proves its address with a Retry first, so that Initials from forged addresses hold at most half. 64 when left out or 0.

address.description: The host and port it listens on, as in ":7000"; an empty host is every address.

cert_file.description: A tls, wss or quic listener's certificate: a PEM file with it, followed by any intermediates, for nodes and proxies that check it with ca_file or the system's roots; with key_file. Read when the hub's member is applied, and again when it changes on disk (fit run -watch-certs). The hub's own certificate, in quic, when left out.

key_file.description: The PEM private key of cert_file.

path.description: A ws or wss listener's path. /tunnel when left out.

protocol.description: The protocol: tls, TCP over TLS; wss, a WebSocket over TLS, for networks that let only HTTPS through; quic, over UDP; or tcp and ws, the same in the clear, which only a loopback address, or a hub with body_password, may take.

allow_hub_services.description: Let the hubs the node registers with set its services, which are the addresses it opens tunnels to, and write them into this member. Off when left out: only this member and the node's own pages set them.

console.description: The node's web pages; none when left out.

dial_timeout.description: How long a connect to a service may take; shorter than a hub's call_timeout, so that the hub hears either way. 5s when left out.

hubs.description: The hubs the node links to and registers with. None when left out: the console's pages add them.

idle_timeout.description: How long a tunnel may carry nothing either way before it is closed. 2h when left out.

max_tunnels.description: The most tunnels open at once, over every hub; a hub's request for one more is refused. 4096 when left out or 0.

meta.description: Anything else the node tells the hubs, which their pages show.

name.description: The node's name, which proxies name to reach its services. The host's name when left out.

services.description: The services the node reaches, and the only addresses it opens tunnels to.

console.description: The proxy's web pages; none when left out.

forwards.description: Local addresses whose connections are tunneled to a node's service.

hubs.description: The hubs the proxy links to and registers with. None when left out: the console's pages add them.

idle_timeout.description: How long a tunnel may carry nothing either way before it is closed. 2h when left out.

max_tunnels.description: The most tunnels open at once, over every forward; a connection past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. 4096 when left out or 0.

meta.description: Anything else the proxy tells the hubs, which their pages show.

name.description: The proxy's name, which the hubs and nodes show. The host's name when left out.

open_timeout.description: How long the opening of a tunnel may take, through the hub to the node and on to the service. 20s when left out.

web_proxies.description: Local addresses that serve a hub's console pages through its encrypted console_socket.

address.description: The service's TCP address, host and port.

description.description: What the service is, for the pages.

name.description: The service's name among the node's, which proxies' forwards name.

body_password.description: The hub's body_password, when it has one. A tcp:// or ws:// endpoint whose host is not a loopback one needs it.

ca_file.description: A PEM file of the CAs that sign the hub's certificate, which tls://, wss:// and quic:// endpoints check it against, its name too, in place of the system's roots. Read at each dial. Not with pin.

call_timeout.description: How long the hub may take to answer a registration or a call. 10s when left out.

dial_timeout.description: How long a link's dial may take. 5s when left out.

endpoints.description: The hub's addresses, in the order each link tries them: it dials the first one not disabled, and the next when that fails.

name.description: The hub's name here, which forwards and the pages name it by. The first endpoint's address when left out.

password.description: The hub's shared password: deprecated for token, taken by hubs of this release with a warning, and refused by the next.

pin.description: The SHA-256 fingerprint of the hub's certificate, as its pages show it, which tls://, wss:// and quic:// endpoints check the certificate against, in place of the chain and name checks: for a hub with a self-signed certificate. Without it or ca_file, the certificate is checked against the system's roots.

ping_interval.description: How often the round trip to the hub is measured. 5s when left out.

ping_timeout.description: How long a ping may go unanswered before it counts as lost. 5s when left out.

pool_size.description: How many links to the hub carry tunnels; each tunnel goes over one throughout. 10 when left out or 0.

quic_insecure.description: Take any QUIC certificate, which lets anyone on the path read and change what the quic links carry: for tests only. Refused for a quic:// endpoint whose host is not a loopback one, unless body_password is set; pin and ca_file override it.

quic_pin.description: Renamed pin; the old name goes in config version 2.

retry_interval.description: How long a link waits after a failed dial, or a lost hub, before it dials again. 3s when left out.

token.description: The token the hub issued for this node or proxy, as fitt1.<id>.<secret>, which its pages, its Admin API module or fit token show once when they make it. Set token or password, not both.

listen.description: The local host and port the pages are served on.

max_conns.description: The most connections open at once; one past it is closed as soon as it is accepted. 32 when left out or 0.

name.description: The hub's name, for the pages.

bind_address.description: How a URL issued for a viewer's address is bound to it: ip, to that address alone, or subnet, to its /24 for IPv4 and its /64 for IPv6, for viewers whose address changes within their network. A URL issued without an address is good from anywhere. ip when left out.

cookie.description: Hands the grant on as the cookie fit_media_grant, on the resource's path and HttpOnly, rather than in the query of every URI a playlist names, for players that drop a playlist's query parameters. The URL the player starts from keeps its query. Off when left out.

max_sessions.description: The most playback sessions one subject may have at once, a session being a URL's sid, playing while it fetches within session_idle; past it, on_limit says what happens. No cap when left out or 0.

max_tracked_sessions.description: The most sessions the policy keeps track of, of all its subjects; a new session past it is answered 503. 100000 when left out or 0.

on_limit.description: What a new session past max_sessions does: refuse, answered 403, or end_oldest, which ends the subject's session that started first, whose next request is answered 403. refuse when left out.

origins.description: The origins whose scripts may fetch the URLs, as referers lists them, matched against a request's Origin: a request with another Origin is answered 403, one without any let through. Any when left out.

play_grace.description: How long the grant a playlist hands its segments, init segments, keys and subtitles lives past the later of the URL's expiry and the item's end, played from when the playlist is fetched: so that a film does not stop halfway, nor after a pause, while the URL itself dies soon. A live stream's grant lives this long past the URL's expiry. 30m when left out.

referers.description: The origins of the pages that may play the URLs, as https://www.example.com or https://*.example.com, * matching any run of characters, matched against the origin of a request's Referer: a request with another Referer is answered 403, one without any let through. Any when left out.

session_idle.description: How long a session may go without a request and still count as playing. 2m when left out.

trusted_proxies.description: The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of fit, whose X-Forwarded-For is believed when a URL bound to an address is checked: the viewer is the last address in it that is not one of them. None when left out: the viewer is the connection's peer.

ttl.description: How long a URL media_tokens' /urls issues is good for when the request names no ttl, and at most the route's max_ttl. 10m when left out.

addresses.description: The addresses of the upstream's servers, each a host and a port, as in "10.0.0.1:8080" or "backend:80".

connect_timeout.description: How long opening a connection may take; 10s when left out. A request whose connect times out gets 504.

deny_internal.description: Refuse to connect where an address, or the address its host name resolves to, is loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, the metadata service of most clouds, among them), unspecified, multicast or the host's own, decided once each connection is open and before anything is sent on it; a request refused so gets 502, as one whose connect fails. For addresses others choose: the Kubernetes provider sets it on the upstreams of ExternalName Services. Off when left out.

fail_timeout.description: The window max_fails are counted in, and how long an address that reached them stays out; 10s when left out.

hash_key.description: With header_hash, the header, and with cookie_hash, the cookie, whose value requests are hashed by.

health_check.description: Probe each address on a schedule, and take one that fails its probes out of rotation until it passes them again; no probes when left out. Probes and max_fails take an address out each on their own account.

idle_timeout.description: How long an idle connection is kept before it is closed; 60s when left out.

load_balancing.description: How requests are spread over the addresses: round_robin, in turn; weighted_round_robin, in turn by weight (smoothly, as nginx does); least_conn, to the address with the fewest requests under way for its weight; random, at random by weight; p2c, to the less busy for its weight of two addresses chosen at random; ip_hash, uri_hash, header_hash and cookie_hash, by a consistent hash of the client's IP address, the request's path and query, the header hash_key names or the cookie it names, so that the same key goes to the same address while it is up, and adding or removing an address moves only the keys that went to it or will. A request without the header or cookie goes in turn. round_robin when left out, or weighted_round_robin when weights are given.

max_conns.description: The most connections open, or being opened, to one address; a request past it waits for one to be free. 256 when left out or 0.

max_fails.description: How many failed requests to an address within fail_timeout take it out of rotation for fail_timeout, as nginx's max_fails does: a connect that failed, an upstream that broke off or timed out. 1 when left out; 0 keeps every address in rotation.

max_idle_conns.description: How many idle connections to one address are kept for later requests; 32 when left out, and 0 keeps none.

max_pending.description: How many requests may wait for a connection to one address once its max_conns are busy; one past it is answered 503 at once. 1024 when left out or 0.

name.description: A name unique among the upstreams, by which handlers refer to this one.

protocol.description: How requests reach the upstream: http/1.1 in the clear, h2c (HTTP/2 in the clear, which the servers must expect), or h2 (TLS, with HTTP/2 when the server chooses it through ALPN and HTTP/1.1 otherwise). http/1.1 when left out.

response_header_timeout.description: How long the upstream may take, once the request is sent, to begin its response; 60s when left out. A request past it gets 504.

response_idle_timeout.description: How long the upstream may go silent in the middle of a response body; 60s when left out.

response_timeout.description: How long a whole response may take, from sending the request to the end of its body; 1h when left out. A request past it before its response began gets 504, and one past it later is cut short.

sticky_cookie.description: Keep each client on one address with a cookie: a request whose cookie names an address that is up goes there, and any other gets the cookie for the address it went to. No cookie when left out.

tls_ca_file.description: With h2: a PEM file of the certificates the servers' are checked against, in place of the system's roots. It is watched, as a listener's certificate files are: a change loads the config again.

tls_cert_file.description: With h2: a PEM file of the client certificate, and the chain after it, that fit presents to servers that ask for one (mutual TLS); needs tls_key_file. It is watched, as tls_ca_file is: a change loads the config again.

tls_key_file.description: With h2: the PEM file of tls_cert_file's private key.

tls_server_name.description: With h2: the name the servers' certificates are checked against, and sent in SNI; each address's host when left out.

weights.description: Each address's weight, in the order of addresses: its share of requests under weighted_round_robin, and how many requests it takes to be as busy as an address of weight 1 under least_conn. 1 each when left out.

media.description: Run fit as a WebRTC media server: the UDP port the PeerConnections of the whip and whep handlers share, the ICE servers told to their peers, and their limits. Routes with whip or whep handlers answer 503 without it. None when left out.

proxy.description: Put media servers behind fit: the UDP port the webrtc_proxy handler's answers name, which relays each peer to the media server that answered it, found by the ICE ufrag of the peer's first STUN request. Routes with webrtc_proxy handlers answer 503 without it. None when left out.

turn.description: Run a TURN server (RFC 8656), which relays UDP for WebRTC peers and other ICE agents that cannot reach each other directly. None when left out.

access.description: The peer addresses the port serves, deciding before the global access: the datagrams of an address it refuses are dropped, so its ICE checks go unanswered. A change applies to the next new address, without starting the media server again; the sessions and addresses served are kept.

codecs.description: The codecs publishers may send, by encoding name: opus, VP8, VP9, H264 and AV1, every one when left out. Each publisher's offer is answered with the first of its codecs of each kind that is listed here, which its viewers must accept.

connect_timeout.description: How long a session may take from its answer to a connected PeerConnection before it is ended. 30s when left out.

ice_servers.description: STUN and TURN servers the peers are told of in Link headers (RFC 9725), for their side of ICE; fit's side needs none, as it is an ICE lite agent on its own address.

ice_timeout.description: How long a connected peer may be silent, its media and ICE consent checks alike, before its session is ended: a publisher's ends its stream and its viewers. 30s when left out.

key_frame_interval.description: The least time between two key frame requests (PLI) passed to a publisher, for the viewers that join or lose packets: the rest are dropped. 500ms when left out.

listen.description: The UDP address every peer's media reaches fit at, one port all PeerConnections share, as in ":8189". A wildcard host advertises the address of every interface that is up, unless public_ips is set. A change starts the media server again, ending its sessions.

max_bitrate.description: The most bits a second a publisher may send: told to it as REMB feedback, which browsers keep under, and enforced with two seconds of burst, past which its packets are dropped. 8000000 when left out or 0.

max_peer_connections.description: The most PeerConnections at once, publishers' and viewers'; one more offer is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0.

max_sdp_bytes.description: The largest offer taken; a larger one is answered 413. 32 KiB when left out or 0.

max_streams.description: The most streams published at once; one more publisher is answered 503. 64 when left out or 0.

max_viewers.description: The most viewers of one stream; one more is answered 503. Each packet a publisher sends is sent again to every viewer, on the worker that received it. 256 when left out or 0.

public_ips.description: The addresses peers are told to reach the port at, with its port, instead of the interfaces' own: a server behind a 1:1 NAT, or a load balancer that forwards the port unchanged. A change starts the media server again.

turn_credential_ttl.description: How long the TURN credentials an answer carries are good for. 1h when left out.

turn_urls.description: URLs of fit's own TURN server, webrtc.turn, as peers reach it, as in "turn:turn.example.com:3478": each answer's Link headers carry them with time-limited credentials made from webrtc.turn's secret, which must be set.

access.description: The peer addresses the port relays, deciding before the global access: the datagrams of an address it refuses are dropped. A change applies to the next new address, without ending a session or relay; the addresses relayed are kept.

idle_timeout.description: How long a relayed peer address may send nothing before its relay is closed, whatever its media server sends it; ICE's consent checks, every 5 seconds or so, keep a live one open. 30s when left out.

listen.description: The UDP address peers reach the media servers behind fit at, one port for them all, as in ":8190": the proxied answers name it as their only candidate. A wildcard host advertises the address of every interface that is up, unless public_ips is set. A change ends every relay and session.

max_relays.description: The most peer addresses relayed at once, each with a UDP socket of its own toward its media server; past it, a new address's STUN request is dropped. A session relays at most 8 of its peer's addresses. 4096 when left out or 0.

max_sessions.description: The most sessions proxied at once; one more offer is answered 503 before it reaches a media server. 4096 when left out or 0.

port_max.description: The highest local port of the sockets toward the media servers; with port_min. The range bounds the relays at once, beside max_relays.

port_min.description: The lowest local port of the sockets toward the media servers, for a firewall in front of them that admits a range; with port_max. A port in use is skipped, and a peer address that finds the range full is dropped. Ports the kernel picks when both are left out. Applies to the next relay.

public_ips.description: The addresses peers are told to reach the port at, with its port, instead of the interfaces' own: a server behind a 1:1 NAT. Applies to the next answer.

relay_ip.description: The address the sockets toward the media servers leave from, one of the host's, for a firewall in front of them that admits one source address, or a host with several interfaces. Of the media servers' family: a media address of the other family is not relayed. The route's pick when left out. Applies to the next relay.

session_timeout.description: How long a session is kept with nothing relayed for it: from its answer until its peer's first request, and after its last relay ends. Its ufrags are forgotten then, and its URL answers 404. 30s when left out.

add.description: Values to add to fields, after any already there.

delete.description: Fields to delete: names, or a prefix ending in "*", as in "X-Debug-*".

set.description: Fields to set, each replacing any of the same name.

module.description: The module's name within its namespace.

address.description: Where the application listens: a host and port, as "127.0.0.1:9000", or "unix/" and a socket's path, as "unix//run/php/php-fpm.sock".

connect_timeout.description: How long connecting may take; 5s when left out. A request that times out connecting is answered 504.

dotfiles.description: Whether scripts whose paths have a segment starting with a dot, as /.git/x.php or /.env, run: deny answers a request for one 404, and try_files passes over it, but /.well-known/ under the root; allow runs them as other scripts. On Windows deny also refuses a script with a segment shaped as an 8.3 short name, as GIT~1 for .git, which NTFS may give a dotfile. The path info after a script is not looked at. deny when left out.

env.description: More parameters for the application, set after fit's own.

idle_timeout.description: How long an idle connection is kept; 60s when left out.

index.description: The script a path ending in / runs; index.php when left out.

max_conns.description: The most connections to the application, each carrying one request at a time. 64 when left out or 0.

max_header_bytes.description: The most bytes the response's CGI header may take; past it the request is answered 502. 64 KiB when left out or 0.

max_idle_conns.description: The most idle connections kept for later requests. 16 when left out or 0.

max_pending.description: How many requests may wait for a connection when max_conns are busy; past it a request is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0.

response_header_timeout.description: How long the application may take to begin its response; 60s when left out.

response_idle_timeout.description: How long the application may go silent in the middle of a response; 60s when left out.

root.description: The document root, which SCRIPT_FILENAME, DOCUMENT_ROOT and PATH_TRANSLATED are made from, as the application sees it.

split_path.description: What ends a script's name in a path, the rest being PATH_INFO: "/index.php/a/b" runs /index.php with PATH_INFO /a/b. A static handler on a file system that folds case serves no file with one of these extensions, in any case. [".php"] when left out.

timeout.description: The most a whole exchange may take; 10m when left out.

try_files.description: Paths tried in turn, as nginx's try_files, for the script to run: {path} stands for the request's path, and the first whose script exists under root runs; ["{path}", "{path}/index.php", "/index.php"] sends what is no script of its own to the front controller, as most PHP applications want. Looked up on a pool of goroutines of its own. Left out, the path runs as it is.

allow.description: The destinations the proxy connects to: host names, "*.example.com" for every name below example.com, IP addresses and CIDR ranges, which also hold the address a host name resolves to. Every destination deny does not hold when left out, but for loopback, link-local (169.254.169.254, the metadata service of most clouds, among them), unspecified and multicast addresses and the host's own, which are refused unless a range here lies inside theirs, as "127.0.0.0/8" does and "0.0.0.0/0" does not, or, for the host's own, names that address alone; others are answered 403, or 502 for a host name whose address decides.

clients.description: The addresses and CIDR ranges of the clients that may use the proxy, as "10.0.0.0/8"; others are answered 403.

connect_timeout.description: How long resolving and connecting to a destination may take; past it the request is answered 504. 10s when left out.

deny.description: Destinations refused, written as in allow, whatever allow holds.

idle_timeout.description: How long a tunnel may carry nothing either way before it and its connection to the destination are closed. 5m when left out.

ports.description: The destination ports allowed; any when left out.

auth.description: The media_auth policy every request, playlist and segment, must satisfy, play on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. A playlist fetched with a token in its query names its playlists, segments and parts with the token too, so that a player that sends no header (Safari, ffmpeg) plays on. With the policy's url_signing, a signed URL of the stream plays too, and its playlists hand what they name a grant of their own. Everyone may play when left out.

cors.description: Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, as "*", for players on other origins. None when left out.

format.description: The segment format of a playlist's URL without a format query parameter: fmp4, fragmented MP4 for H.264, H.265, AV1, AAC and Opus, or ts, MPEG-TS for H.264, H.265, AAC and Opus. The other is played with ?format=ts or ?format=fmp4. fmp4 when left out.

idle_timeout.description: How long a stream's segmenting runs without a request before it stops. 30s when left out.

max_bytes.description: The bytes of segments one stream and format holds; the oldest go first. 32 MiB when left out or 0.

part_duration.description: Turns on Low-Latency HLS with parts this long, 200ms to 1s being usual: blocking playlist reloads, EXT-X-PART and preload hints. Off when left out.

play_wait.description: How long a playlist request may wait for a stream with no publisher yet. 404 at once when left out.

playlist_size.description: How many segments a playlist lists. 6 when left out or 0.

prefix.description: The part of the path before the stream's: with /hls/, /hls/live/cam/index.m3u8 is the playlist of live/cam. / when left out.

target_duration.description: How long segments are: a stream with video is cut at the first key frame after it. Set it to the key frame interval. 2s when left out.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a player must satisfy, play on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter (/live/cam.flv?token=T) or the fit_media_token cookie. 401 with a Bearer challenge without credentials, 403 when they do not allow it. With the policy's url_signing, a signed URL of the stream plays too. Everyone may play when left out, as the route's middleware allow.

cors.description: Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, which a web player on another origin (flv.js, mpegts.js) needs, as "*". None when left out.

prefix.description: The part of the path before the stream's: with /flv/, /flv/live/cam.flv plays live/cam. / when left out: /live/cam.flv plays live/cam, the stream rtmp://host/live/cam publishes.

wait.description: How long a player may wait for a stream with no publisher yet, or for the next one after its publisher leaves. 404 at once for a stream without a publisher when left out.

auth.description: The media_auth policy the room API checks, and the pages' login and tokens belong to: joining a room and following it needs play on <room>-*, announcing that one publishes publish on <room>-<name>, as the WHIP and WHEP endpoints the pages use check with their own auth, which should name the same policy. Everyone may use the room API when left out, as the route's middleware allow.

cam_default.description: Whether a member's camera is on when it joins a call in the pages: off when left out, for the member to switch on, and a publisher sends a frame with its name while it is off, so a switch never renegotiates. The URL's cam=0 or cam=1 overrides it.

channels.description: List the streaming role's channels on the library page too, those the viewer may play, with what each plays now and next, played from hls, which must be set, through a playback URL signed for the viewer as an item's is. Off when left out.

chat.description: Whether a room call has a chat: the pages show it, and the room API carries the members' text messages and small files between them. False answers the chat's API 404 and shows no chat window. True when left out.

hls.description: The URL of a stream's HLS playlist, {stream} standing for its name, as /hls/{stream}/index.m3u8 for the streaming role's hls handler: the play page plays it where the browser plays HLS itself, with the page's token. None when left out.

ice_servers.description: STUN and TURN servers the pages' PeerConnections use, as a browser's iceServers. None when left out: fit's media server is an ICE lite agent that browsers reach directly, and tells them of its own ICE servers in its answers' Link headers.

libraries.description: The media_library names whose items the library page lists, at most 16: those the viewer may play, play on vod/<library>/<id> under auth, that can be served, with their posters, searched and paged; the player page plays one with hls.js, vendored in the binary. With the auth policy's url_signing, and playing not public, the player plays through a playback URL the pages sign for the viewer, its address and a session of its own, good for url_signing's ttl, whose playlists hand the player its grant; otherwise through the plain URL, which the login's cookie lets in. None when left out: no library page.

links.description: Further URLs the publish and play pages show for a stream, for tools outside the browser, as the streaming role's RTMP, RTSP, SRT and HTTP-FLV ones: {stream} stands for the stream's name, {token} for the page's token, {host} for the host the page was loaded from.

login.description: Show a login form for the users of the auth policy: a right password is answered with a token the policy signs, for its token_ttl, set as the HttpOnly cookie fit_media_token (SameSite=Strict, Secure over TLS), which the WHIP, WHEP and HLS requests of the pages carry, and handed to the page too. Without it the pages ask for a token instead, as fit media-token prints, when auth needs one.

max_file_bytes.description: The largest file a member may send in a room's chat, in bytes; a larger one is answered 413, and the page refuses it before sending. 5 MiB (5242880) when left out.

max_members.description: How many members a room may have; a join past it is answered 503. A room may have twice as many watchers, its members' event streams among them. 16 when left out.

max_message_bytes.description: The largest body a request of the room API or the login may have, in bytes; a larger one is answered 413. 1024 when left out.

max_rooms.description: How many rooms may have members or watchers at once; a join or a watch past it is answered 503. 64 when left out.

member_ttl.description: How long a member stays in its room without a heartbeat: the pages send one every third of it. 30s when left out.

mic_default.description: Whether a member's microphone is on when it joins a call in the pages: off when left out, for the member to switch on, and a publisher sends a silent track while it is off, so a switch never renegotiates. The URL's mic=0 or mic=1 overrides it.

pages.description: Serve the pages: the index, the call, the publish and the play pages, and their script and style. False serves none of them: their paths answer 404, for a deployment whose page is its own; the login and the room API stay, for that page. True when left out.

prefix.description: The path the pages are served under, which the route must match with what is below it, as /media/* beside /media; a request outside it gets 404. /media when left out.

stall_timeout.description: How long a room's event stream may wait for its browser to take what it was sent before it is cut off. 30s when left out.

title.description: The pages' title; fit media when left out.

vod.description: The URL of an item's multivariant playlist, as a vod handler serves it, {library} standing for its library's name and {id} for its ID: a path on this server or an http or https URL, ending in {id}/ and the playlist's name. The item's poster is beside it, poster and its extension. /vod/{library}/{id}/index.m3u8 when left out, the vod handler's own prefix.

whep.description: The URL streams are played from with WHEP, {stream} standing for the stream's name. /whep/{stream} when left out.

whip.description: The URL streams are published to with WHIP, {stream} standing for the stream's name: a whip handler's, or stream_whip's for the streaming role, on this server or another. /whip/{stream} when left out.

auth.description: The media_auth policy that signs the tokens, as whip's auth names one: it must set secret_file, or a keyring whose keys each set secret_file, so that a revoke can rotate a secret file and outlive a restart.

max_body_bytes.description: The largest request body the route takes; a larger one is answered 413. 64 KiB when left out.

max_tokens.description: The most tokens one request may ask for; more is answered 400. 100 when left out.

max_ttl.description: The longest a request may ask a token to be good for; a longer ttl is answered 400. 24h when left out.

prefix.description: The path the route serves under: the route must match it and what is below it, as /media-tokens and /media-tokens/*; a request outside it gets 404. /media-tokens when left out.

prefixes.description: The stream-name prefixes this route may sign for: every publish and play pattern of a request must start with one of them, so that a token cannot be signed for a stream outside them, as mtg- for mtg-42-*. Any valid pattern when left out.

revoke_timeout.description: How long a revoke may wait for the secret file's write before it is answered 504; the write, one at a time on a pool of its own, never blocks a worker. 10s when left out.

url_base.description: What the URLs <prefix>/urls answers start with, before their paths: the scheme and host viewers reach fit's vod, hls and httpflv routes at, as https://media.example.com. The paths and their queries alone when left out.

url_prefixes.description: The path prefixes <prefix>/urls may sign URLs for: every path of a request must start with one of them, as /vod/films/, so that a URL cannot be signed for a resource outside them. Any path when left out.

failover.description: An upstream that takes the requests when none of the chosen upstream's backends is in rotation, for failing or for its health checks, and one of its own is.

host_header.description: The Host header sent upstream; the client's when left out.

mirror.description: Send a copy of a share of the requests whose bodies arrive whole (64KB at most) to another upstream, and drop its answers. At most 256 copies are under way at once; past that, requests are not copied. The requests themselves do not wait for their copies.

retry.description: Send a request that failed again, to the backend the upstream picks next: one whose connection could not be made, whatever its method, and, for GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT and DELETE, one that failed before its response began or was answered with a status of statuses. A request whose body streams (past 64KB, or still arriving) is never sent again. No retries when left out.

splice_uploads.description: On Linux, move a large upload (128KB or more, framed by its Content-Length) from a client's HTTP/1.1 connection without TLS to an HTTP/1.1 upstream without TLS with splice(2), the kernel passing its pages from one socket to the other, rather than copying it through the proxy. An upload that cannot go so, to an h2, h2c or TLS upstream, or chunked, goes the ordinary way. It costs the proxy about 40% less CPU on such uploads and the upstream about 5% more, which reads the body cold rather than as the proxy just wrote it, and more once the upstream itself is the bottleneck: false suits an upstream whose CPU is scarcer than the proxy's. False copies every upload. True when left out.

timeout.description: The most a request may take, from when the proxy takes it to the end of its response, retries included: one past it before its response began is answered 504, and one whose response is under way is cut short. None when left out.

trusted_proxies.description: The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of this one, whose X-Forwarded-* and Forwarded fields are believed. None when left out.

tunnel_idle_timeout.description: How long a tunnel, as a WebSocket the proxy has joined to its upstream is, may carry nothing either way before it is closed; 10m when left out.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream requests go to; or upstreams.

upstreams.description: Upstreams requests are spread over at random by weight, as a canary release does, in place of upstream.

headers.description: Response headers. Content-Type defaults to text/plain; charset=utf-8 when there is a body.

status.description: The status code; 200 when left out.

browse.description: List a directory that has no index file, rather than answering 404. Files whose names start with a dot are left out.

browse_max_entries.description: The most entries a listing reads and shows; a directory with more is listed in part, and says so. 10000 when left out or 0.

check_interval.description: How long what the handler learned of a request path, the file it names and its validators, is trusted before the disk is looked at again, where no watch reports its changes. On Linux a watch of the directories under the root reports a change within moments, a file written, replaced or removed, a directory renamed, or a symbolic link on the way to the root pointed elsewhere, and what it watches is trusted until it does; this interval is for other systems, and for a file that is a symbolic link, whose target's changes the watch does not see. A file is told by its size, modification and status change times and inode, so one replaced by another of the same size and modification time is seen too. 0 looks at the disk for every request, with no watch, so that a response always carries the file as it is on disk then, also on a network file system, whose changes from other machines no watch sees. 5s when left out.

dotfiles.description: Whether files and directories whose names start with a dot, as .git, .env and .htpasswd do, are served: deny answers a request for one, or for anything under a dot directory, 404, as for a file not there, but /.well-known/ under the root, for ACME's HTTP-01 challenge and security.txt; allow serves them as other files. Listings leave them out either way. On Windows deny also hides a path with a segment shaped as an 8.3 short name, as GIT~1 for .git, which NTFS may give a dotfile. deny when left out.

index.description: The files that stand for a directory, tried in order; ["index.html"] when left out, and none for [].

max_cache_bytes.description: How many bytes of files are kept in memory at most; 64 MiB when left out.

max_file_bytes.description: The largest file kept in memory, in bytes; 1 MiB when left out.

precompressed.description: Encodings whose compressed twins, name.br, name.zst and name.gz, are served in place of a file to a client that accepts them: the one it prefers by Accept-Encoding, and among equals the first listed. None when left out.

root.description: The directory files are served from. On a file system that folds case, as Windows' and macOS' do by default, a request whose path is not written as the names on disk are, or for a file whose extension a fastcgi handler's split_path names, in any case, is answered 404, so that a route matching names, as \.php$, is not passed by.

strip_prefix.description: A prefix removed from the request path before it is looked up under the root; a request whose path lacks it gets 404.

try_files.description: Paths tried in turn for a request, as nginx's try_files: {path} stands for the request's path, and one ending in / for a directory, served by its index file. The first that exists is served, and when none does the answer is 404; ["{path}", "{path}/", "/index.html"] serves a single-page app. A directory asked for without its slash is not redirected then.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy, play on the stream's path, as stream_whip's. A session's URL takes PATCH and DELETE without credentials. Everyone may play when left out.

prefix.description: The part of the path before the stream's. /whep/ when left out.

stream.description: The stream's path. When left out, it is the path after prefix a POST is sent to, as live/cam in /whep/live/cam. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy, publish on the stream's path: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. 401 with a Bearer challenge without credentials, 403 when they do not allow it. A session's URL takes PATCH and DELETE without credentials, its random ID being the capability (RFC 9725). Everyone may publish when left out, as the route's middleware allow.

prefix.description: The part of the path before the stream's. /whip/ when left out.

stream.description: The stream's path. When left out, it is the path after prefix a POST is sent to, as live/cam in /whip/live/cam. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too.

auth.description: The media_auth policy every request, playlist, segment, subtitle and file, must satisfy, play on the stream vod/<library>/<id>: a bearer token, Basic, the token query parameter or the fit_media_token cookie. A playlist fetched with a token in its query names its playlists, segments and subtitles with the token too, so that a player that sends no header (Safari, ffmpeg) plays on. With the policy's url_signing, a signed URL of the item plays too, and its playlists hand what they name a grant of their own. Everyone may play when left out.

cache_control.description: Sent as Cache-Control with every playlist, segment, subtitle and file, so that a CDN keeps them, as "public, max-age=86400": they change only when their file does, which their ETag and Last-Modified say. None when left out.

container.description: The segments of index.m3u8: fmp4, fragmented MP4 for H.264, H.265, AV1, AAC and Opus, or ts, MPEG-TS for H.264, H.265, AAC and Opus, for older players. Either is played by its own name too, index.fmp4.m3u8 and index.ts.m3u8. fmp4 when left out.

cors.description: Sent as Access-Control-Allow-Origin, as "*", for players on other origins. None when left out.

encrypt.description: Encrypts the segments with AES-128 (METHOD=AES-128), fMP4 and MPEG-TS alike, each item under a key of its own derived from the library's secret, which the media playlists name as aes.key in the item's directory and the handler serves only to a request auth lets play that item: segments copied, as a CDN keeps them, do not play without it. The files themselves are then not served; initialization sections, subtitles and posters stay clear. Needs auth and the library's secret or secret_file. Off when left out.

library.description: The media_library whose items are served.

max_cache_bytes.description: The most memory the handler keeps of what it builds from the files, for the next request: how each is cut into segments, its playlists, its segments and subtitles, the least recently used dropped; and of what it is building. 256 MiB when left out or 0.

max_segment_bytes.description: The largest segment: one that would be larger is cut at an earlier keyframe, or without one when there is none. 64 KiB to 1 GiB, and at most a quarter of max_cache_bytes. 32 MiB when left out or 0.

prefix.description: The part of the path before an item's ID: with /vod/films/, /vod/films/films/bbb/index.m3u8 is the playlist of the item films/bbb. /vod/<library>/ when left out.

segment_duration.description: About how long segments are: a file with video is cut at the keyframe nearest this after a segment's start, so set it to the keyframe interval the files were made with, or a multiple of it. 1s to 60s. 4s when left out.

timeout.description: How long a request may wait for what it needs to be read and built on the library's file pool; past it the answer is 503. 30s when left out.

action.description: What an offer asks of auth: publish for a WHIP endpoint, play for a WHEP one. Required with auth.

auth.description: The media_auth policy an offer must satisfy before it is sent to a media server: its credentials need action on the stream, the last segment of the POST's path, which must then be 1 to 128 letters, digits, '.', '_', '~' and '-', decoded, or the offer is answered 400. Missing or bad credentials are answered 401 with a Bearer challenge, others 403. A session's URL is passed on without credentials, its ID being the capability; the request's Authorization goes on to the media server as it came. Everyone may when left out, as the route's middleware allow.

max_sdp_bytes.description: The largest request and answer passed on, an offer and an answer among them; a larger request is answered 413, and a larger answer 502. 32 KiB when left out or 0.

media_addrs.description: The address fit relays a media server's peers to, by the media server's address in the upstream, as {"10.0.0.2:8080": "10.0.0.2:8189"}, or an IP alone, which takes the port of its answer's candidate. When left out, the answer's first host candidate, or server-reflexive one, IPv4 first.

timeout.description: The most a request may take, from its last byte to the media server's answer read whole; past it, it is answered 504. 10s when left out.

upstream.description: The upstream of the media servers, picked by its load balancing for each offer: fit's own whip and whep, or any WHIP or WHEP server. Its health checks and timeouts apply.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy to play the stream: its credentials need play on the stream's name, or the policy makes play public. Missing or bad credentials are answered 401 with a Bearer challenge, others 403. A session's URL takes its DELETE without credentials, as whip's. Everyone may play when left out, as the route's middleware allow.

stream.description: The stream's name. When left out, the name is the last segment of the path a POST is sent to, as cam1 in /whep/cam1 on a route of /whep/*: one route plays every stream. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too, as /watch/* beside /watch.

auth.description: The media_auth policy a POST must satisfy to publish the stream: its credentials, a bearer token or a user and password, need publish on the stream's name, or the policy makes publish public. Missing or bad credentials are answered 401 with a Bearer challenge, others 403. A session's URL takes its DELETE without credentials: its ID, 128 random bits, is the capability. Everyone may publish when left out, as the route's middleware allow.

stream.description: The stream's name. When left out, the name is the last segment of the path a POST is sent to, as cam1 in /whip/cam1 on a route of /whip/*: one route takes every stream. A session's URL is the path of its POST followed by its ID, which the route must match too, as /live/* beside /live.

module.description: The module's name within its namespace.

forward_authorization.description: Leave the Authorization field, with the password, on the request the handler sees; it is removed when left out.

realm.description: The realm the browser shows when it asks for a user and password; fit when left out.

user_header.description: A request field to set to the user's name for the handler, and the upstream a proxy sends the request to; any the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, is replaced.

users.description: The users allowed in, with their passwords' bcrypt hashes.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes a request's body may have.

default_ttl.description: How long a response is fresh for when it gives no lifetime of its own (no s-maxage, max-age or Expires) and its status allows one to be assumed (200, 203, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414, 501): in place of a tenth of the time since its Last-Modified, at most a day, which is used when this is left out.

disable_lock.description: Lets every request that misses fetch for itself. When left out, a request that misses while another fetches the same response waits for that fetch, up to lock_timeout, and is answered from what it keeps (a cache lock), so that many requests for a response not kept make one fetch.

disk.description: A disk tier for the zone: every response kept in memory is written to disk too, on a pool of goroutines of its own, and one the memory no longer holds is read back from disk, on that pool, and kept in memory again. None when left out. Caches of one zone take the disk of the last one loaded.

lock_timeout.description: How long a request waits for another's fetch of its response before it goes on to fetch for itself. 5s when left out.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes the zone keeps in memory, bodies, fields and keys counted; past it the least recently used responses go. 128 MiB when left out or 0. Caches of one zone take the size of the last one loaded.

max_entry_bytes.description: The largest body kept; a larger response goes to its client without being kept. At most a sixteenth of max_bytes. 1 MiB when left out or 0.

max_entry_size.description: Renamed max_entry_bytes; the old name goes in config version 2.

max_size.description: Renamed max_bytes; the old name goes in config version 2.

stale_if_error.description: How long past its lifetime a response may still be answered when fetching it again fails, with no response or a 500, 502, 503 or 504, for a response that does not say how long itself (Cache-Control stale-if-error, RFC 5861). None when left out.

stale_while_revalidate.description: How long past its lifetime a response may still be answered while the cache fetches it again in the background, for a response that does not say how long itself (Cache-Control stale-while-revalidate, RFC 5861). None when left out. A response that says must-revalidate, proxy-revalidate or s-maxage is never answered stale.

zone.description: The store responses are kept in. Caches of the same zone, in one route or several, share it, its size and its keys; it is kept across reloads while a cache uses it. default when left out.

error_ratio.description: The share of failures in the window that opens it; 0.5 when left out.

half_open_requests.description: How many requests it lets through, half-open, that must all fare well for it to close; 5 when left out. Others are answered 503 meanwhile.

min_requests.description: How many requests the window must have counted before it can open; 20 when left out.

open_duration.description: How long it stays open before letting requests through to try; 30s when left out.

slow_ratio.description: With slow_threshold, the share of slow responses in the window that opens it; 0.5 when left out.

slow_threshold.description: A response that takes longer than this to begin counts as slow; none is when left out.

statuses.description: The statuses that count as failures; 500 to 599 when left out.

window.description: How far back requests are counted, in ten steps; 10s when left out.

optional.description: Let a request without a certificate through as well, unauthenticated; refused with 403 Forbidden when left out.

subject_header.description: A request field to set to the certificate's subject, as in "CN=alice,O=Example", for the handler and the upstream a proxy sends the request to; any the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, is removed, with or without a certificate.
