encodings.description: The encodings offered, the one the client prefers most chosen, and among those it prefers as much, the first here; zstd, br and gzip when left out.

level.description: How hard the compressors work: fastest, default (gzip 5, zstd's default, brotli 4) or better (gzip 7, zstd's better, brotli 6); default when left out.

max_in_flight.description: How many responses are compressed at once; past it, responses go uncompressed, so that the compressors' memory, a few hundred kilobytes each, is bounded. 1024 when left out.

min_bytes.description: The shortest declared body compressed; 1024 when left out. A body that declares no length, as one that streams, is compressed.

min_length.description: Renamed min_bytes; the old name goes in config version 2.

max.description: The most requests under way at once.

status.description: The status of a request refused; 429 when left out, or 503 as nginx's limit_conn answers.

copy_headers.description: Fields copied from a 2xx answer onto the request, for the handler and the upstream a proxy sends it to. Any of these the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, are removed, so that it cannot pass them off as the auth service's.

request_headers.description: The request's fields sent to the auth service; all but the hop-by-hop ones and those of the body when left out.

timeout.description: How long to wait for the auth service's answer, after which the request is answered 504 Gateway Timeout; 10s when left out. A service that cannot be reached is answered 502 Bad Gateway.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream the auth service is.

uri.description: The path, and query, of the request sent to the auth service; / when left out.

request.description: Changes to the request's fields, made before the handler, and the upstream a proxy sends the request to, sees them.

response.description: Changes to the response's fields, made just before it is sent, whichever handler wrote it.

algorithms.description: The algorithms tokens may be signed with; any that fits the keys when left out. none never is.

audience.description: Audiences of which a token's aud must name one; any when left out.

claims_headers.description: Request fields to set to claims, as {"X-User": "sub"}: a string as it is, anything else as JSON. Any of these fields the client sent, also spelled with _ for -, are removed, with or without the claim.

hmac_secret_file.description: A file whose contents are the secret of tokens signed with HS256, HS384 or HS512; at least 32 bytes.

issuer.description: The iss a token must have; any when left out.

jwks_refresh.description: Renamed jwks_refresh_interval; the old name goes in config version 2.

jwks_refresh_interval.description: How often the JWK set is fetched again; 1h when left out. A token naming a kid the set does not have has it fetched sooner, at most every 10s.

jwks_url.description: The URL of a JWK set (RFC 7517) whose signing keys tokens are verified with.

leeway.description: How far exp and nbf may be off, for clocks that differ; none when left out.

public_key_files.description: PEM files of public keys or certificates (RSA, ECDSA or Ed25519) tokens are verified with.

token_from.description: Where the token is: header, after Bearer in the Authorization field; header:Name, the whole of that field; cookie:name; or query:name. header when left out.

burst.description: How many requests a key may make at once, after it has been idle: the bucket's size. The rate, rounded up, when left out.

ipv6_prefix.description: How many leading bits of an IPv6 client address name the client with key ip: a host is given a /64 to pick its addresses from, so counting each address apart would let it make a fresh key with each request. 64 when left out or 0; 128 counts each address apart.

key.description: What requests are counted by: ip, the client's address; route, every request of the route together; or header:Name, a header's value, with a request without it counted by ip. ip when left out.

max_keys.description: The most keys kept at once, which bounds the memory the buckets take: under 100 bytes each, and up to 128 more for a header; 100000 when left out or 0.

rate.description: How many requests a second each key may make, on average; at least 0.001.

status.description: The status of a request refused; 429 when left out.

trusted_proxies.description: The addresses ("10.0.0.1") and networks ("10.0.0.0/8") of proxies in front of fit: for a request that comes from one, the client's address is the last in X-Forwarded-For that is not one of them. None when left out, and the client is the connection's peer.

regexp.description: A regular expression in Go's syntax that the path, as escaped ("/a%20b", "/a%2Fb"), must match for the request to be redirected; the rest go on to the handler. Every request is redirected when left out. A URL made from the request that would leave the site, which to does not, is answered 400: one that starts with "//" or "/\", and, when to starts with a group ($1), one with a scheme.

status.description: The status: 301 and 308 are permanent, 302, 303 and 307 temporary; 307 and 308 keep the method and body. 302 when left out.

to.description: Where to: a URL or a path, in which {scheme}, {host} (with its port, as the client sent it), {path}, {query} (without the '?') and {uri} (the path and query) stand for the request's, and, with regexp, $1 or ${name} for its groups, as in "https://{host}{uri}" or "/new/$1".

add_prefix.description: A prefix put before the path, as in "/v2".

regexp.description: A regular expression in Go's syntax; each match in the path is replaced with replacement.

replacement.description: What replaces each match of regexp, in which $1 or ${name} stand for the regexp's groups.

strip_prefix.description: Prefixes to take off the path: the first that the path starts with, at a segment boundary, is removed, and what is left starts with '/'. "/api" makes "/api/users" "/users" and "/api" "/", and leaves "/apix" alone.

config.description: A string the plugin reads, for settings of its own.

instances.description: How many instances of the plugin run calls at once, each with its own memory: the CPUs fit has, at most 16, when left out or 0.

max_body_bytes.description: For a Proxy-Wasm plugin given the response's body, how much of it the plugin may hold, pausing it to see more, or make it; past it the response fails, or goes on without the plugin when on_error is skip. 1 MiB when left out or 0.

max_memory.description: Renamed max_memory_bytes; the old name goes in config version 2.

max_memory_bytes.description: The most memory an instance may have; one that asks for more fails its call. 128 MiB when left out or 0.

max_streams.description: For a Proxy-Wasm plugin that follows responses, how many an instance follows at once, each keeping its context; past it a request is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0.

on_error.description: What a call that fails, traps or runs past its timeout leads to: fail answers 500, or fails a response under way, closing its HTTP/1 connection or resetting its stream; skip lets the request or its response go on as if the plugin were not there. fail when left out.

path.description: The plugin: a WebAssembly module that exports fit_on_request, as a WASI reactor; package plugin/wasm/guest builds one from Go with GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm go build -buildmode=c-shared.

properties.description: For a Proxy-Wasm plugin, properties it reads by their path (proxy_get_property), beside the request's own: request.path, request.url_path, request.query, request.host, request.method, request.scheme, request.protocol, source.address and plugin_name.

queue.description: How many requests may wait for an instance; past it a request is answered 503. 1024 when left out or 0.

response.description: For a Proxy-Wasm plugin that exports response callbacks, which it is given: all, the header, the body and the trailer; headers, the header alone, the body going by untouched; none, none of them, the plugin forgetting each request once it has gone on. all when left out.

timeout.description: How long a call may run; past it the call is stopped and its instance replaced, and the request goes as a failure does (on_error). 100ms when left out.

vm_config.description: For a Proxy-Wasm plugin, its VM configuration, which it reads as it starts; config is its plugin configuration.

wait_timeout.description: How long a request may wait for an instance; past it it is answered 503. 1s when left out.

name.description: What the URL is, as RTMP or SRT.

url.description: The URL, with {stream}, {token} and {host} filled in by the page.

percent.description: The share of requests copied, chosen at random; all of them when left out.

upstream.description: The name of the upstream the copies go to.

attempts.description: How many times a request may be sent again after the first; 2 when left out.

budget_min_per_second.description: Retries allowed each second beyond budget_ratio, so that a proxy taking few requests may still retry; 10 when left out.

budget_ratio.description: Retries may add at most this share of the requests the proxy takes, so that retries cannot multiply the load on an upstream already failing; 0.2 when left out.

statuses.description: Statuses of the upstream's, 5xx ones, that have a request of an idempotent method sent again, as 502, 503 and 504; none when left out, so that only requests that got no response are.

weight.description: Its share of the requests, against the others' weights.

path.description: The property's path, by segment, as ["route_metadata", "filter_metadata", "envoy.filters.http.wasm", "auth"].

access.description: The client addresses fit serves, by allow (whitelist) and deny (blacklist) lists, for every listener, route, service and role that sets no access of its own that decides: a more specific one, set on a listener, route, service or role, decides first, and this one only for an address that one has no say on. Every address is served when left out.

access_log.description: Where a line is written for each request, as JSON or, as its format says, text or line; no access log when left out.

acme.description: How certificates for the names listeners list in tls.acme are obtained and renewed; the defaults when left out. Its settings are read when fit starts: a change to them takes effect when fit restarts. The names follow every reload.

admin.description: The Admin API, through which the running config is read and replaced, and which serves metrics in Prometheus's text format at /metrics; off when left out. Its settings are read when fit starts: a change to them takes effect when fit restarts.

auto_https.description: HTTPS by default: a config that writes no listeners is served over HTTPS on port 443, with certificates obtained with acme for the host names its routes match, and over HTTP on port 80 only to be redirected; a listener whose tls is empty gets certificates for the host names of the routes it serves. On when left out.

engine.description: How fib, the network engine fit serves and dials on, is set up: its event loops, workers and buffers. fib's own defaults for what is left out, and for all of it when engine is. Read when fit starts: a change takes effect when fit restarts.

limits.description: Limits that apply to every listener.

listeners.description: The addresses fit listens on, and the protocols each one serves. When left out, HTTPS by default makes them from the routes' host names; see auto_https.

llm.description: The LLM feature's roles to run beside the gateway, on its engine: a hub, a node and a proxy, which share AI models among machines and serve them to agents. None when left out. What their web pages change is written back here.

log.description: fit's own log: what it says about starting, reloading, certificates, providers and the engine, by logger, each with the least level written, and the format and output it writes in, as fib writes its own. Messages at info and debug to stdout and the rest to stderr, at info and above, as lines, when left out.

media_auth.description: Named policies of who may publish and play which streams, with tokens, users and keys for tokens fit signs: the handlers and roles that take media (whip, whep, webrtc_proxy) refer to one with their auth param. A handler without auth lets everyone in, as the route's middleware allow.

media_library.description: Named libraries of media files: directories scanned into a catalog of items, each a title with its renditions, audio, subtitles and poster, probed off fib's workers on a bounded file pool of the library's own, and read by the Admin API's /media/library. None when left out: no files are scanned or served.

metrics.description: Count and time requests by listener and route, for the Admin API's /metrics, which serves the rest of fit's metrics without it; off when left out, since it costs every request a little. Needs admin.

pprof.description: Serve Go's runtime profiles, as net/http/pprof does, at the Admin API's /debug/pprof/: CPU, heap, allocations, goroutines, blocking, mutexes and execution traces, for go tool pprof and go tool trace. Off when left out: the endpoints answer 404, and blocking and mutexes are not sampled. Follows every config applied, with no restart. Needs admin; served on the Admin API's own address, behind its token, and not through the console.

providers.description: Sources of routes, upstreams, services and listeners other than this file and the Admin API, merged into the config: what this config writes wins over every provider, and a provider over those listed after it; a provider's element named as one before it is left out. The Admin API's /config/effective shows the result and where each part came from. Read when fit starts: a change takes effect when fit restarts.

routes.description: How requests are matched, and what handles them.

schema_version.description: The version of fit's config this one is written for, 1; fit refuses a config written for a version it does not read, rather than read it wrongly. Optional: a config that leaves it out is read as version 1.

services.description: Layer 4 services: the upstreams the connections of tcp listeners are proxied to, byte for byte, and the datagrams of udp listeners, one for one.

streaming.description: fit's streaming role, beside the gateway on its engine: one media hub where a stream is published once, over RTMP, RTSP, SRT or WHIP, and played over any of them, HTTP-FLV and HLS too, each listener and handler with its media_auth policy. None when left out.

telemetry.description: OpenTelemetry: traces of requests, with W3C trace context sent on to upstreams, and metrics, exported over OTLP/HTTP to a collector. Neither when left out. Read when fit starts: a change takes effect when fit restarts.

tunnel.description: The tunnel's roles to run beside the gateway, on its engine: a hub, a node and a proxy, which reach services behind NAT through the hub. None when left out. What their web pages change is written back here.

upstreams.description: The servers requests can be proxied to, by name.

webrtc.description: What fit runs for WebRTC beside the gateway, on its engine: a TURN server, the media port of the whip and whep handlers, and the relay of the webrtc_proxy handler. None when left out.
